meaning_mnemonic: In your fingers is a weapon, so you throw it. Maybe you're angry and you threw the weapon at a person you don't like. Maybe you're a pacifist and you threw it away so no one else could use it. Either way, when you have a weapon in your fingers you have to throw it.
reading_mnemonic: You throw your weapon away because you're about to enter とうきょう and there are no weapons allowed there. There is, however, a big pile of thrown away weapons by the border, which is where you're throwing yours right now.

meaning_mnemonic: You have at your disposal a tsunami to assassinate this person, or a hook. Which method will you choose? Decide now!
reading_mnemonic: To remember the けつ reading, we always use the word "ketsup." It's a special mix of ketchup and catsup (yum): You finally decide. You're going to go with the tsunami... but not just any tsunami. You'll kill him with a tsunami of ketsup (けつ).

meaning_mnemonic: You dig a hole nine times for your research. You should always do research with nine variables so you can compare them, and so there's an uneven number.
reading_mnemonic: Your research is on cucumbers (きゅう)!

meaning_mnemonic: The radical and the kanji are exactly the same, so this means someone.
reading_mnemonic: If you don't know who someone is, odds are they're a shaman (しゃ). Only a shaman would have the mystical powers to obscure their own identity and pass themselves off as a mysterious, unknown "someone."

meaning_mnemonic: A stone lantern is an excellent way to sharpen anything, even in the dark. Your knives, your forks, your spoons, and even your sword.
reading_mnemonic: Why did you sharpen your blade? Because you are about to do battle with Ken (けん), the famous samurai warrior.

meaning_mnemonic: The horse radical and the horse kanji are exactly the same! Huzzah!
reading_mnemonic: You are looking at a horse. It's looking at you. You try making horse noises at it, to get a reaction. Instead of reacting with a normal horse noise, it just makes sheep noises: "Baaa," (ば) it says. "Baaaaa."

meaning_mnemonic: Dirt makes it easy to identify your location. Even if you add an extra line to mark the ground, it's still easy. Keep that in mind and you can go from place to place.
reading_mnemonic: Knowing your location from dirt is quite a feat! Who taught you that? It was Joe (じょう), the big local farmhand. Despite being a bit weird, he can identify any place just from its dirt!

meaning_mnemonic: There's a cross sticking out the top of the sun and another cross sticking out the bottom. The moon is off to the right. That's because it's the morning, which is when the sun and moon switch over. Those crosses are making sure the sun stays high in the sky for the rest of the day.
reading_mnemonic: Every morning you have Asahi (あさ) beer for breakfast.

meaning_mnemonic: You have to sickle the rice paddy today because it's your turn. This kanji also means number in a series, which is a lot like a turn. For example, you're number 3, so your turn will be number 3.
reading_mnemonic: This turn-based rice sickle system is a contest as well! But, you are disappointed to find out that you have been banned (ばん) from the game because of the performance enhancing steroids you've been taking.

meaning_mnemonic: "Does the bamboo shirt suit me?" you ask... but nobody will answer.
reading_mnemonic: You pull out a quarter (こた) and offer it to whoever will give you an answer.

meaning_mnemonic: When a bunch of threads are meeting on paper (after you've dipped them in paint, say) they can create a masterpiece of a picture (or painting).
reading_mnemonic: You tell someone you painted this masterpiece of a picture. Their response? "EH (え)?!"

meaning_mnemonic: Here's a net full of of shellfish that you can buy. You can't just buy loose shellfish. You can only buy the ones that are in the net, bagged up and ready for your money.
reading_mnemonic: You decide to buy as many shellfish as you can fit in your car (か). You keep buying until your car is completely full of shellfish before you stop. Cars are totally a realistic unit of measure.

meaning_mnemonic: Aim the scooter's neck at the road! Scooters are only meant for driving on streets and paths, and if you go the wrong way, you'll probably break your own neck!
reading_mnemonic: To remember the reading どう we use the word "doughnut." You're traveling down this road so fast that you don't see the giant doughnut (どう) that's rolling toward you until the last minute. You crash into it, and both you and the doughnut go tumbling down. Ahg, your neck!

meaning_mnemonic: There's a gate that the sun goes through at a regular interval. There is an interval of time in the sense that the sun goes through it at the same time every day. And there is an interval of space in the sense that it has to go through the space between the gate posts.
reading_mnemonic:
This method of keeping track of intervals of time was invented by the great Khans of Mongolia, specifically the most famous Khan of all: Genghis Khan (かん).

Genghis Khan has had a huge impact on the world as we know it, especially the Eurasian continent of the past, so he's going to come up a lot from now on. Be prepared to get very familiar with him and his friends!

meaning_mnemonic: Give rice to a woman in winter so she can count it. The woman will count each individual grain of rice, then tell you the amount or number of grains.
reading_mnemonic: Why do you have to count your rice out like this? It's because someone sued (すう) your farm and took everything you owned. Since being sued, you only have a small amount of rice to last the winter.

meaning_mnemonic: The white ice tree is a magical tree that radiates an aura of comfort, ease, and pleasure, with its icy foliage tinkling like beautiful music whenever it sways in the breeze.
reading_mnemonic: You want more of this aura of comfort, so you chop down the magic tree and build a clothing rack (らく) out of it. Then, you put the rack in your house so you can enjoy that fuzzy feeling of comfort and ease every time you go to hang something up.

meaning_mnemonic: Say it with your tongue. If you do, you'll be able to talk. You'll be able to speak.
reading_mnemonic: If something uses their tongue, it will be able to talk and speak. To prove this, you teach a walrus (わ) to use its tongue, and lo and behold, it speaks to you!

meaning_mnemonic: You're in the rain, in a rice paddy, holding an umbrella. You're here because there's nothing else that's very tall around you. You want to get hit by electricity (aka lightning), to prove that it exists.
reading_mnemonic: After the electricity hits you, you feel your face. In it is a huge dent (でん).

meaning_mnemonic: You're tearing this door down with an axe. You're absolutely crazy. "I HATE THIS PLACE!!" you keep yelling as you smash in the door.
reading_mnemonic: You smash through the door and finally get inside the place, only to find some kind of show (しょ) going on. It's a circus show — elephants, tightrope walkers, bears on unicycles! The greatest show on earth, but why is it at this place?

meaning_mnemonic: You find a cross in the mouth of Wolverine. What a strange occurrence. I guess he put it there, but why would he do such a thing? You ask him, but he says it's a personal matter of utmost secrecy.
reading_mnemonic: This occurrence doesn't impress Jesus (じ), who appears and gently removes the cross from Wolverine's mouth.

meaning_mnemonic: A good leader can put the ground's history to great use. You are a good leader. You have studied the ground and dirt of the earth your entire life. You know the history of the ground and you know how to use it to lead your people.
reading_mnemonic: You use the ground to raise sheep (し). When you were down there sniffing around you realized that your people will flourish best if you use this land for grazing and raising sheep.

meaning_mnemonic: There's an eye on the ground, among some fins. What happened? You killed a fish, and now you must hide the murder tool. Quick, hide the tool before someone finds out it was you.
reading_mnemonic: The tool is dripping with goo (ぐ). Goopy, incriminating goo. It's the guts of the fish you just killed and it's all over your hands too. Yuck.

meaning_mnemonic: Someone throws a cleat at your forehead while you sit on a stool. You must accept this. Then another guy cleats you in the forehead, but you remain on the stool and receive it without complaint. This is some kind of acceptance ritual for the most prestigious Spanish soccer club in the world. If a cleat to the forehead doesn't knock you off the stool, you'll receive an offer to join.
reading_mnemonic: After they accept you, they give you a small juice (じゅ) box. It's to help you recover from the trauma of getting kicked. And you receive the juice with grace.

meaning_mnemonic: When everyone has grain in their mouth, you will have peace. That is the Japanese style of doing things.
reading_mnemonic: Peace is the Japanese style. The walruses (わ) living off of Japan see this, and start to emulate.

meaning_mnemonic: If you give a woman a machine she'll begin learning how to use it right away. She'll also get it to start before anyone else could. Women are really good at starting up new machines!
reading_mnemonic: Actually, before she can begin, she has to shear the sheep (し) over there. The machine is going to turn wool into yarn, but you can't just start that process by shoving the sheep in there. You have to keep the little sheep safe!

meaning_mnemonic: You build a roof over your coat rack because you determine that this is the best way to protect your coats from the elements.
reading_mnemonic: Why did you determine your coat rack needed a roof? Because your coat pockets are full of tater (てい) tots! You can't afford to let your tater tots get rained on, so you determined they needed to be properly sheltered with a roof.

meaning_mnemonic: Climb onto the roof in spring to see the truth. The world is waking back up from winter and revealing the reality of what it is all around you.
reading_mnemonic: At the moment, you're trying to learn the truth about the deer that is coming out of the snowy woods when you see not one, but two baby deer appear with it! Gee! Two (じつ) babies! You keep looking around and realize that all of the animals seem to have two babies that they had hidden in the snow.

meaning_mnemonic: Take the moon stamp on the stool in front of you and use it on all of your clothes. Now even if you sell or lose a piece of clothing, you'll be able to find it again by checking for your special moon stamp.
reading_mnemonic: A few days later you're with a friend when you recognize the clothes they're wearing. You grab it, rip it off, and scream, "F**k (ふく) you!" There is your moon stamp! These are your clothes!!

meaning_mnemonic: If a tsunami is going to last an eternity you better learn how to swim now. We'll be under water for the rest of time and if you can't swim you're not gonna make it.
reading_mnemonic: Oy (およ)! Oy, stop daydreaming about swimming and actually do it!

meaning_mnemonic: A cow with wings is flying in the air. What a strange thing! You've heard of flying pigs before, but cows? This is a new and strange thing indeed! Cows with wings! What a silly thing.
reading_mnemonic: You want a thing to help you fly with the cow so you put on your flying boots (ぶつ). Your flying boots are a pretty strange thing in themselves, but they're the only way you can keep up.

meaning_mnemonic: The flowers have grown old, so they're suffering.
reading_mnemonic: If a flower or a person is growing old and suffering, give them a cookie (く).

meaning_mnemonic: Sometimes life gives you a kick, and you have to express yourself to deal with it! How do you express yourself? On the surface (of your face)!
reading_mnemonic: You need to express yourself, so you call up a friend and say "Heyo!" (ひょう).

meaning_mnemonic: The clown building is over in that part of town. We keep the clown part as separate as we can from the rest of the normal people. In fact, the entire clown education department and their clown clubs have to stay in their part, they can't come in ours.
reading_mnemonic: You see, that part of town is full of booze (ぶ). Clowns need a lot of booze to keep their charade going, so we just let them have it. But they aren't allowed in our part anymore, because they all stink of nasty clown booze.

meaning_mnemonic: You put a grain in your mouth and let it take a ride. This kanji has the same radicals as 和, but this time the grain is in your mouth, which is why there's little pieces of grain sticking out of the 口 part ;)
reading_mnemonic: You decide the grain is probably lonely on this ride alone, so you add some nori (の) seaweed, so it has a friend.

meaning_mnemonic: Under your roof in winter there are more mouths to feed because you let guests stay with you when it's cold. Some of them aren't family, so they have to pay to stay under your roof and get food. Those are customers.
reading_mnemonic: One of your guests is a regular named Kyaku (きゃく) the customer. Kyaku is always staying over at one place or another, so everyone knows their name.

meaning_mnemonic: You plant a flag in the ground, marking your private patch of dirt. In this spot you raise a roof, then fill the space beneath it with some shops and stores.
reading_mnemonic: The roof covering the dirt is there so that the Yankees (や) can play baseball year round. The stores and shops are there to sell hot dogs and Yankees memorabilia.
radical_breakdown: 尸|Flag, 一|Ground, ム|Private, 土|Dirt

meaning_mnemonic: A yurt's stool is always placed at certain degrees. The degrees change depending on specific occurrences.
reading_mnemonic: Also angled at exact degrees is the dog (ど).

meaning_mnemonic: People who loiter around the temple are probably just trying to wait. They don't mean to look like they're up to no good, but it's hard to wait without looking suspicious when you're waiting outside a temple.
reading_mnemonic: As you wait outside the temple, you can't help but adjust your tie (たい). When you wait you get nervous, and when you get nervous you fidget. So now you're messing with your tie a whole bunch.

meaning_mnemonic: You need to get your fingers around a temple if you want to hold it. Is the temple too big? Hold smaller temples you can buy in the temple's souvenir shop.
reading_mnemonic: As you hold the temple you hear a voice. You look down through your fingers and see a tiny Jesus (じ). He's smiling and gives you a thumbs up. Aww, thanks Jesus!

meaning_mnemonic: Every rice paddy sits jammed in to the world.
reading_mnemonic: To get around this world of rice paddies, you need to use a kayak (かい).

meaning_mnemonic: Go to the tent and take the lantern from it, then we will be ready for departure. We can't leave the lantern inside of the tent; that's a fire hazard. We'd best take it with us before the departure. Don't you agree?
reading_mnemonic: Oh! Don't forget your hats (はつ) either. Wouldn’t want to start a departure without hats or a lantern. That'd be a short journey.

meaning_mnemonic: You need to look a tree in the eye to gain a mutual respect for each other. Stand up straight, look the tree directly in its eye(s). If it looks right back, you know things are mutual.
reading_mnemonic: If your respect for the tree is mutual with the respect the tree feels for you, you'll be able to see the tree's soul (そう). Right now its soul looks pretty sad, like it's trying to say, "Why are your people cutting down all my friends? I thought we had a mutual understanding."

meaning_mnemonic: The eye of a lion, still small and curious, gazes upon the prefecture that will one day become his. He's a small lion, but once he grows up, everything reflected in his eye will be his prefecture to rule over.
reading_mnemonic: This small lion's prefecture is being protected by Ken (けん) the samurai, because the lion is too small to protect all of this land himself. Ken the samurai is used to wandering far and wide, so one prefecture is nothing to him.

meaning_mnemonic: A sheep that's big is a true beauty. Big is beautiful, and that's all the more true for sheep.
reading_mnemonic: The big sheep's beauty has attracted a swarm of bees (び). The sheep is so beautiful that the bees have mistaken it for a flower.

meaning_mnemonic: When you're in prison, whoever ends up with the shellfish will lose. It's the game all prisoners play. It's like keep away from the shellfish. And if you end up with the shellfish BZZZZTT that's it, you're the loser.
reading_mnemonic: If you lose, you're a fool (ふ). All you had to do was not hold the prison shellfish. It really shouldn't have been that hard to not lose, ya fool.

meaning_mnemonic: On its scooter, a creature with horns from heaven will take things you want to send there.
reading_mnemonic: You want to send your soul (そう) to heaven. I mean, you don't want it to go to some of those other places you've heard of, so why not send your soul?

meaning_mnemonic: The heavy radical and the heavy kanji are the same.
reading_mnemonic: In your hand is a very heavy jewel (じゅう). Real jewels are always heavier than they look.

meaning_mnemonic: You say things around a fire. In fact there are two fires, and you're talking with a group of people, all sitting around two nice campfires.
reading_mnemonic: You talk in this intense, fiery way all the way until dawn (だん), but no longer! Once dawn comes the discussion needs to be concluded.

meaning_mnemonic: When a helicopter is piloted by a woman, it stirs an insatiable need in her. She doesn't know what it is. But she needs it. And that's why she's flying around looking for it!
reading_mnemonic: Finally she knows what she needs! It's yogurt (よう)! Delicious, creamy yogurt!

meaning_mnemonic: The moon grants a gladiator its power so he will win! Victory will be his!
reading_mnemonic: He wins over and over again, and soon the Shougun (しょう) is even rooting for him. In fact, the Shougun claims him as his personal gladiator of choice.

meaning_mnemonic: Run into oneself in a dream and you'll definitely wake up.
reading_mnemonic: If one runs into oneself and you don't wake up, just look down at your waist. If you're wearing an obi (お) you know it's a dream and you'll eventually wake up. If you aren't wearing an obi then it isn't a dream and you don't have anything to wake up from.

meaning_mnemonic: You jump on your scooter with a big bundle to go as fast as you can! You have a bundle of pizzas in here, and they need to be delivered as fast as you can get them there!
reading_mnemonic: You were going so fast, you only put on socks (そく). So now you're barreling down the street at top speeds in just your sad, white socks.

meaning_mnemonic: You don't want to keep all the alcohol to yourself (oneself), so you distribute it to all of your friends. Heck, not just your friends, to everyone you can find!
reading_mnemonic: As you distribute the alcohol you say a haiku (はい): Here you go my friends Alcohol for everyone Never drink alone

meaning_mnemonic: A tsunami is an alcoholic beverage containing a lot of alcohol. It’s 3 different kinds of rums, pineapple juice, and grenadine. It’ll hit you like a tsunami though. This alcoholic drink has a kick to it.
reading_mnemonic: As you lie on this beach, the alcohol keeps coming down a chute (しゅ), straight into your mouth. You can feel the sand in your toes and the alcohol sliding down your throat from this special tsunami chute.

meaning_mnemonic: This building has a roof and will teach you about the origin of many things. It's an institution!
reading_mnemonic: What does institution start with? In (いん)!

meaning_mnemonic: The thread of winter and ice has brought this year to its end. Once you're in the long thread of winter and ice, you know the year will end soon.
reading_mnemonic: Whenever winter ends, you take the thread covered in ice, and lace it into your shoe (しゅう).

meaning_mnemonic: You find some feathers that are so perfectly white, you want to learn more about where they came from and what they're made of.
reading_mnemonic: You learn that you should tie these white feathers to your shoes (しゅう). You do it before you learn what it will do, and then suddenly you're jump-flying out of the building.

meaning_mnemonic: If your car runs into a cloud you'll revolve around it instead of going straight through. Clouds are really hard to see through, so even though you're trying not to, you revolve in a tight circle up and around the cloud anyway.
reading_mnemonic: You have to revolve around the cloud ten (てん) times before it disappears and you're able to go through.

meaning_mnemonic: You give your scooter to a turkey so that it can advance. The turkey was trying and failing to walk through a crowded street, so out of the goodness of your heart you gave it a scooter so it could advance.
reading_mnemonic: You wave as the turkey advances into the street at top speeds, collides with a car, and scrapes up its shins (しん) almost immediately. Ah!

meaning_mnemonic: Flowers are knocked down by a violent tsunami, and swirl through the air to kiss your face gently as they fall. With the tsunami came a great windy storm that blew the flowers down. Amongst all the destruction, it's a pretty sight to watch them fall.
reading_mnemonic: You want to save these flowers that fall around you, so you take out a drying rack (らく) and place them carefully on it. Any flowers that fall will go on the rack like this, so can save them for later.

meaning_mnemonic: Flowers bring beauty to the world of trees, but the leaf is what matters the most. Leaves are how flowers and trees get their nutrients from the sun!
reading_mnemonic: Picture a little flower working really hard to grow its first leaf. The leaf pops out and it shouts, "Ha (は)!"

meaning_mnemonic: While riding your scooter, you bang your forehead on the car in front. Your scooter's wrecked, so you have to carry it home. You'll need a lot of luck to get that scooter home safely.
reading_mnemonic: As you carry the scooter, your luck turns, and it starts to rain, so you pull out your umbrella (うん). Now you're holding your scooter, your forehead, and an umbrella.

meaning_mnemonic: A gate with a lantern is open for you. That's convenient, since it's pretty dark out and you might not have seen the open gate without the lantern's help.
reading_mnemonic: This open gate is in the water though, so you'll need a kayak (かい) to get in. Luckily, you've been carrying your kayak with you just in case.

meaning_mnemonic: You chase a turkey up a tree to collect it. At least, you will once you've gathered enough turkeys into this one tree.
reading_mnemonic: Once you've collected enough turkeys, you're going to turn them into a shoe (しゅう). Maybe even two shoes, but that will mean gathering even more turkeys!

meaning_mnemonic: You can eat all you want, but you'll still lack something to drink. You can't live just from eating, you have to drink things too!
reading_mnemonic: You get desperate for a drink and put some nori (の) seaweed in a blender, trying to create a drink of your own.

meaning_mnemonic: You have spikes growing out of a sheep with fins. Turn this thing into a business! You could totally charge people money to look at it. Sure, you could also donate it to science, but a business-minded person like you knows a business opportunity when you see one. Step right up! Just five dollars for a glance at the rare spiky mer-sheep!
reading_mnemonic: As you evolve your business, you let customers feed the sheep gyoza (ぎょう) dumplings, its favorite snack. For a nominal fee, of course. People love it when the mutant sheep eats gyoza out of their hands. Wouldn't you?

meaning_mnemonic: A tsunami hit ancient China and formed the Chinese country we know now as... China! Sometimes this kanji also means man. In fact, it used to refer specifically to people of the Han dynasty, but over time evolved into a term for men in specific contexts.
reading_mnemonic: You peer closer at China and see one man, Genghis Khan (かん), leading his troops into the vast country, ready to conquer all the Chinese people living in China!

meaning_mnemonic: If you've been walking all day, your foot is the last thing anyone would want to kiss, especially after wandering barefoot down a road. Your feet are filthy, sweaty, and stinky. Nobody is going to want to kiss those feet.
reading_mnemonic: What was this person walking down again? Oh, that's right – a road (ろ). They were walking down a filthy road.

meaning_mnemonic: You blast your music loud so it causes a landslide, revealing the perfect soil for farming! Musically moved dirt is perfect for agriculture.
reading_mnemonic: The first person to come up with this farming method was Nostradamus (のう), the famous seer and prophecy man. He predicted humans of the future would use special "yell cubes" to "move that good earth."

meaning_mnemonic: If a lip ring (or two in this case) is what you lack, it's going to be way easier for you to sing a song.
reading_mnemonic: Where are you always singing songs, by the way? In your car (か). It's not just you, either. Pretty much everyone likes to sing in their car.

meaning_mnemonic: If someone sticks bamboo in your eye twenty times, the first thing your brain does is calculate how painful it is. Your brain's pain calculation will determine how you calculate your next move.
reading_mnemonic: Next you want to calculate how much punishment your bamboo attacker deserves, so you call on Santa-san (さん). Santa-san is always calculating how many pieces of coal the naughty children deserve, so he's perfect for this calculation job.

meaning_mnemonic: If you go up to a gate and press your ear to it, you'll hear what's going on on the other side. The people on the other side will have no idea you can hear their conversation.
reading_mnemonic: From the other side of the gate, you hear one of the people start to play a song on a recorder. You recognize the song as "Hot Cross Buns (ぶん)." You haven't heard this song since grade school. "Hot cross buns, hot cross buns~"

meaning_mnemonic: What you say between five mouths is a language. As long as there are five different people saying these same words with their five mouths, it's considered its own language.
reading_mnemonic: Another mouth joins in speaking the language, but it's green and scaled and... it's Godzilla's (ご) mouth! Godzilla speaks this language too.

meaning_mnemonic: You have to say what you’re selling because people don’t like to read. If they walk right by and don’t read, you better say what you have for sale so they’ll know! Read it out loud to them.
reading_mnemonic: What are you forced to read aloud to sell? Yo-yo (よ) instructions! You’d think they’d be self explanatory, but there are actually a lot of rules and tricks that you have to read to get good at yo-yoing. Read all of these out loud so you can sell them.

meaning_mnemonic: When the mouth of a bird opens, you're most likely to hear a chirp. This is how birds communicate. They open their mouths and let out a series of chirps. Chirp chirp chirp!
reading_mnemonic: The best way to experience the chirp-chirping of birds is to offer them nachos (な). Birds love nachos so much, it's a guaranteed way to make them chirp with delight.

meaning_mnemonic: You can use a long piece of thread during white water rafting as a safety line. Sure it's thin, but if someone goes overboard even a line of thread is better than nothing. Throw them a line and drag them back aboard!
reading_mnemonic: The person who threw you that line of thread is actually a centaur (せん). How kind of him. After you are safe you hop on the centaur's back and ride around to get the wind to dry you off.

meaning_mnemonic: The tree marked with a yellow X on the side of the house is going to get cut down. You’ve marked it with a yellow X so the hired help knows which tree to cut down. There are a lot of trees on the side of the house, but the tree marked with a yellow X is the only one in danger of causing damage to your roof in the event of a storm.
reading_mnemonic: Wait, that woman with the chainsaw is Yoko (よこ) Ono! Yes, the same Yoko Ono who’s married to John Lennon of the Beatles. What’s she doing chopping down trees on the side of your house? Who can say. Silly Yoko.

meaning_mnemonic: You say something about the circumference of this area. You've looked around this whole area, making a big circle around it, because you are trying to investigate something that happened here. You also say this thing in a really quiet tone of voice, because you don't want the person or thing you're investigating to know you're on to them.
reading_mnemonic: "I came here to investigate this place, and I did indeed find out who the criminal is... it's none other than Mrs. Chou (ちょう)!"

meaning_mnemonic: If you're standing under a tree and you see your parent, it's a good chance for a moment of intimacy.
reading_mnemonic: Standing under the tree, you go to give your parent a big hug, but you manage to bang your shin (しん) on a huge tree root. Your parent pulls you in for a warm hug and rubs your shin. Despite the pain, it becomes an unforgettable "shin-timate" moment.

meaning_mnemonic: If you feed a lot of beans to a geoduck, its head will grow larger. To a geoduck, beans are a brain food, so by eating beans, it can grow an incredibly large head. Geoducks already look strange enough as it is, let alone with engorged heads.
reading_mnemonic: As the geoduck eats more and more beans its head gets bigger and bigger, until finally the head explodes like an atomic (あたま) bomb. BOOM! Geoduck parts go flying everywhere and pieces of its massive head float to the ground as atomic fallout.

meaning_mnemonic: You stand on a cliff, a hair's breadth away from the edge, when out of nowhere a geoduck slaps you in the face. The force makes you back away from the edge of the cliff, and your face is all slimy from the geoduck's residue.
reading_mnemonic: But where did that geoduck come from? As you turn from the cliff edge, you find yourself face-to-face with a cow (かお). This cow is the one who hit you in the face with a geoduck. You don't know why, but something about your face has upset the cow.
radical_breakdown: 立|Stand, 厂|Cliff, 彡|Hair, 頁|Geoduck

meaning_mnemonic: A sick stick of dynamite is going to be sick forever. Unfortunately there are no medicines that are effective on sticks of dynamite, so once they contract a sickness, they’re sick for good.
reading_mnemonic: Being nervous all the time about spontaneously exploding would probably make you sweat profusely. And you know what sweating causes? B.O. (びょう). You’d be one smelly stick of dynamite. B.O. is a very unpleasant smell, and being sick is no excuse.

meaning_mnemonic: Let the sun shine into your ear while sitting on a stool and make sure most of it gets in your head. You want to fill your brain with the most sun anyone ever has.
reading_mnemonic: Most of this is for your cyborg (さい). You're testing out a new way to power it, but if you can't get most of the sun into your ear, it won't be enough to power most of the cyborg's robo-parts.

meaning_mnemonic: In prison, Wolverine gets picked on for the barbs coming out of his hands. This creates a lot of conflict between him and the other prisoners. They don't take kindly to mutants, and Wolverine doesn't take kindly to bigots — hence the conflict.
reading_mnemonic: This constant conflict between Wolverine and the other inmates is really affecting his soul (そう). Despite what people think, Wolverine really doesn't like to fight. He just hates injustice so much, he feels he has to do something about it.

meaning_mnemonic: The leader has a cloud that he uses to transmit all of the messages he needs to send to his people. The cloud floats above him and when he wants to tell people something he just whispers into the cloud and it transmits his message really, really loudly to all of them.
reading_mnemonic: As the leader transmits his latest series of messages to you and the others, you notice a pretty large dent (でん) in it. That dent is probably a clue to what this cloud is really made of.

meaning_mnemonic: The card game fish are best at is blackjack because they can easily hold the cards with their fins together. In blackjack you don't have to have a huge hand, full of cards. It's just a few, so fish fins can keep them together and just hit or stay.
reading_mnemonic: Once a year trillions of fish get together in きょうと to play blackjack. They have a huge tournament there once a year.

meaning_mnemonic: There is a woman and a child in front of you. You like them very much.
reading_mnemonic: "I like you two," you say to the woman and child. They both turn their heads 180 degrees back towards you. They both have faces that look just like こういち's. "We like you too," they say in unison.

meaning_mnemonic: When a drunkard holds a sword it becomes something else. The drunkard doesn't become a swordsman, they're still just a drunkard. But the sword in their hands does.
reading_mnemonic: The sword has become a saber (せい)! It's just like the saber you have! Hey, wait.

meaning_mnemonic: By the time you finish digging a coffin hole with nothing but a spoon, you’ll be an old elderly person. Digging with nothing but a spoon takes a long time, especially when the hole needs to be big enough for a coffin. You might as well be digging it for yourself at this rate. By the time you finish, you’ll be all wrinkled and elderly and just about ready to keel over.
reading_mnemonic: Now that you’re elderly (and probably about to die) you suddenly crave some delicious roe (ろう). Salmon roe, sea urchin roe, tofugu roe, doesn’t matter. Your old, tired bones need roe after all that hard work!

meaning_mnemonic: A leader stands at the highest rank in an organization. The leader is of the highest rank and stands above all others.
reading_mnemonic: This great leader is actually the leader of the boy scouts. And as we all know, the highest rank in boy scouts is the rank of eagle (い) scout. This great leader has attained the rank of eagle scout and stands above all other scouts.

meaning_mnemonic: The leader of your clan wants to live close to the ground so he demands you get low. Low, low, with your belly to the ground. That way you're always below him, since he's the leader.
reading_mnemonic: Low people like you can only eat low food like potatoes. But that's boring, so you low people learned to make tater (てい) tots. You roll them to each other and eat them without lifting your heads.

meaning_mnemonic: You wear a special outfit and equip a sword whenever you do something for the first time. Doing something for the first time is always scary, but the right outfit and a sword at your side can give you the confidence and courage to overcome your jitters!
reading_mnemonic: So, what is it you're doing for the first time? A fashion show (しょ). Your special outfit and sword aren't just to calm your nerves — they're also what you'll be showing off on the catwalk.

meaning_mnemonic: In your mouth you put a sword and a knife. Now that you have them in there, you have to make them separate from each other.
reading_mnemonic: Why are you trying to make a sword and knife separate in your mouth? Because someone bets (べつ) you can't do it.

meaning_mnemonic: Cut grains with a knife to make them smaller and you'll make a great profit. By cutting them, now you can get three grains worth of money for what was once a single grain.
reading_mnemonic: To make an even better profit, you decide to cut up reeds (り) too. You stuff the grains in the reeds and sell that as "self-cooking" sets.

meaning_mnemonic: A woman sits on a stool to conserve her power, as her servants toil away in the kitchen. They toil away preparing a feast for this powerful woman while she kicks back on her cozy stool. She's a queen and deserves to be pampered.
reading_mnemonic: As a servant you toil not just for the woman, but also for her dog (ど). Anything she gets, the dog gets too. That means double the toil for you. But hey, at least the dog is cute.

meaning_mnemonic: A Viking in a position of power does not need to labor in the fields. Labor is for the weak! A Viking of power takes what he wants, and need not labor for it. A powerful Viking plunders all and takes what he wants!
reading_mnemonic: It takes a lot of labor to harvest roe (ろう) so that’s what the Viking decides to take first! Roe is delicious, but it’s small and delicate. Vikings don’t labor for their own roe! They take it and eat it!

meaning_mnemonic: Orders coming from your mouth will determine the fate of your soldiers. You are their commanding officer and your orders determine their life and death.
reading_mnemonic: You are the commanding officer on the Mayflower (めい). You give orders to colonize America. The orders spewing from your mouth hole determine the fate of the settlers and the fate of America and the fate of the world! You and the Mayflower have changed everything forever.

meaning_mnemonic: As the year starts moving in the direction of winter, the trees must release their leaves.
reading_mnemonic: The trees release all of their leaves onto your home (ほう). Slowly, you watch in horror as your home is consumed by the released leaves. They enter in through the windows, doors, and the chimney.

meaning_mnemonic: You've been playing blackjack in the sun since long ago. This is the longest game of blackjack you've ever played and it feels like ages since you started. You've been sitting out in the sun playing blackjack since long, long ago.
reading_mnemonic: Once you finally finish the game, you walk the long walk back home, in the sun, barefoot, on a dirt road that hasn't been maintained since long ago. Your feet are all sweaty from being out in the sun, and walking on this dirt road gives you muck ashi (むかし). Your ashi (feet) are all mucky and muddy from the combination of dirt and sweat. Your muck ashi are really gross, man.

meaning_mnemonic: A tsunami master has the power to pour water wherever he pleases. Tsunami masters are masters over the most powerful water force in the universe, so it makes sense that they have the ability to pour water at will, wherever they please. Best not tick off the master, unless you want a tsunami poured on your head.
reading_mnemonic: If Chewbacca (ちゅう) was trying to attack you, you’d be able to defend yourself easily. Simply pour a tsunami on him and Chewbacca would surrender in a heartbeat. Chewbacca doesn’t like having water poured on him, especially not all the water from a tsunami.

meaning_mnemonic: Give trash to the moon and it will nurture and raise that trash like it's its own little moon baby.
reading_mnemonic: The moon nurtures the trash ball until one day, it speaks! "行く (いく), 行く！" it says. It wants to go live with mom moon!

meaning_mnemonic: Try to use your fingers to spoon out some of the sun and you'll come back with just one finger.
reading_mnemonic: Don't worry, you aren't the only one out there with just one finger, sheep (し) only have one finger too. I mean, they're hooves, which are really just a single animal finger. It's just big and kind of flat.

meaning_mnemonic: This tsunami is ridden by a sheep in classic Western style. And by Western style I mean the sheep is dressed in a cowboy outfit and has put a saddle atop the tsunami wave to ride it. It's a tsunami rodeo and this crazy sheep is riding that tsunami wave in classic Western style. This kanji also means ocean, because presumably the people from the West, with their Western style, came from across the ocean. You'll want to be familiar with both meanings for vocab later on.
reading_mnemonic: After a whole day of riding this tsunami, the sheep is hankerin' for some Western-style food, namely yogurt (よう). Yogurt is Western-style food, right? If it helps you can imagine the yogurt is flavored like apple pie, to make it more American and Western.

meaning_mnemonic: Your spirit should feel humble before a god's spirit. You never really feel humble in front of anyone else, but if you meet a god's spirit… Well, you should probably lower yourself appropriately. Gods have powerful spirits.
reading_mnemonic: When you meet a god's spirit, you need to get down on your shins (しん). Get down on your ankles? No, not low enough. Knees? No, no, get your shins flat on the ground to show how humble you really are. Luckily, you're wearing jeans (じん), so at least that will stop your poor shins getting chafed!

meaning_mnemonic: On a scooter there is a bear with a drop on its head trying to follow and chase you! You accidentally splashed it with water and it's not happy about it. You're on your own scooter, luckily, but that doesn't make this any less terrifying.
reading_mnemonic: The bear is trying to follow you because it wants your obi (お) as compensation for its injured pride. The obi is waving in the wind behind your scooter, and the bear is reaching out with its teeth to try and grab it.

meaning_mnemonic: A simple drunkard starting a war.
reading_mnemonic: The simple drunkard started a war with the centaurs (せん)! This is especially unfortunate, because the centaurs are really good at battles because they're all automatically cavalry troops.

meaning_mnemonic: A drop of water to a root is good. It's good for the roots to grow and live and thrive. And what's good for roots is good for our plants and us humans too.
reading_mnemonic: A good way to get a lot of drops of water for your roots is to buy a row boat (りょう). Then just row out to the middle of the lake and plonk all the roots right into the source!

meaning_mnemonic: This cow temple is special. This cow must have been very important to have an entire temple dedicated to it.
reading_mnemonic: This cow is special because it belonged to Tokugawa (とく) Ieyasu, the first shōgun of the Tokugawa shogunate and uniter of Japan! He's a super important figure in Japanese history. You should absolutely look him up and read a bit about him (when you're caught up on these lessons, that is).

meaning_mnemonic: A leader stands upon the ground of the rice paddy. She is searching for treasure. It is said that this treasure here in this rice field will make things much easier for the leader (that's what leaders really want, after all). If she gets this treasure, it will be a great convenience for her, because convenience is everything when you're the leader.
reading_mnemonic: She finds a place to dig in the ground. It looks like there's some fresh dirt here. Finally, the treasure of convenience that will make this leader's life so much easier. She digs into the ground and pulls out a box. When she opens it, she finds out it's a bento (べん). "My god," she thinks. "This really will make my life more convenient. My people can take their lunches with them now instead of coming back to base to eat, which will waste way less time!"
radical_breakdown: ｲ|Leader, 一|Ground, 田|Rice Paddy, メ|Treasure

meaning_mnemonic: Your leader makes you lift heavy loads with all your power, since this is what you do for work. Why do you do this kind of work? Well, you're good at it and the leader makes you do it, I guess.
reading_mnemonic: Where do you get the power to do all this work? From doughnuts (どう). You eat nothing but doughnuts. If you had no doughnuts, you couldn't work. In fact, your leader pays you for your work… in doughnuts.

meaning_mnemonic: The sound of your heart gives me an idea. The methodic thump thump thumping of a heart puts me in a trance that gives me great ideas. It’s a very inspirational sound, the sound of a heart is. It gives me an idea. Alternatively, you could look at this kanji and see a "stand" radical and something that kind of (almost) looks like the kanji for "think." When you stand up and think, you come up with your very own ideas!
reading_mnemonic: The heart of an eagle (い) is very strong. The person who knew this probably came up with the idea to make the bald eagle a symbol of the United States. Eagles are always flying around and doing things, so their hearts are very strong.

meaning_mnemonic: In your mouth there is a jet dropping flavor bombs. Every time you taste something, it's actually because a tiny jet has flown into your mouth to bomb you with flavor.
reading_mnemonic: And what has more flavor than a big slab of meat (み)? You love meat and its flavor nearly as much as you love the taste of its juice. So many good things to put in your mouth!

meaning_mnemonic: You'll have to excuse me, having all this power puts a lot of strain and exertion on my body. My power comes from exertion of muscle, so please excuse me if I start to perspire.
reading_mnemonic: Excuse me, I don’t think I’ve introduced myself yet. My name is Ben (べん) and I use powerful muscle exertion to accomplish every task. Ben knows what Ben wants and how to get it. Remember that, kids.

meaning_mnemonic: There's a canopy and a man called the Yoga King standing in the middle of your garden.
reading_mnemonic: Not only is this Yoga King taking over your garden, but he's ordering you to serve food to his class. "You there, peasant, fetch these people your freshest tater (てい) tots from this puny garden to give them strength."

meaning_mnemonic: Imagining one’s self without a heart can make it hard to draw breath. Without a heart, you’d have no blood pumping and you would start to die. This would make it increasingly harder to draw breath and get oxygen to stay alive.
reading_mnemonic: You know how when people are unconscious and their breath slows or comes to a stop, they use smelling salts to revive them? Well a smelly sock (そく) can work just as well. Socks get really stinky and their stench is powerful enough to revive someone who isn’t drawing breath.

meaning_mnemonic: The direction your gun is facing leads straight to a block of tofu. This might be a sign you need to take a trip. If you're out there pointing guns at tofu, you're probably a little… tired… and in need of a change of scenery. Take a trip!
reading_mnemonic: So, where do you go on your trip? To Rio (りょ). You had to go way down south to get as far away as possible from tofu. Ahh, nothing like a nice trip to Rio!

meaning_mnemonic: A tsunami lifts all the trash out of the river and it streams out onto the shores.
reading_mnemonic: Next to the trash stream you suddenly see Ryu (りゅう) from Street Fighter and he looks pissed. He's furious that so many people throw their trash in the river and it causes streams like this.

meaning_mnemonic: A long time ago a huge tsunami swept a triceratops up into the moon and extinguished its life.
reading_mnemonic: This famous event where almost all life was extinguished is reenacted every year for the Shougun (しょう). He's got a bit of an unhealthy obsession with extinguishing life...

meaning_mnemonic: Even a mouth-bearing shellfish is a member of the invertebrate family. Yes, shellfish do have mouths, look it up!
reading_mnemonic: If you were a member of the same shellfish family, you'd be able to go to the special shellfish inn (いん). Every species has a members-only inn.

meaning_mnemonic: A bird sits upon a mountain. If you look at the radicals, the bird is quite large and the mountain quite small. Think of this in the mnemonic as well. The reason the mountain is small is because you can only see the top of it, sticking out of the water. On it is the bird. This small mountain with the bird on it is an island.
reading_mnemonic: But this island doesn't only belong to the bird. In fact, the bird shouldn't be on this island, because it belongs to the Sheep Mama (しま), who is like Mother Nature but for sheep. The all-powerful Sheep Mama comes to kick the bird off the island, because this place is only for sheep! All hail the Sheep Mama.

meaning_mnemonic: Someones and buildings, someones and buildings, someones and buildings. So many someones and buildings. With so many someones and buildings, we have ourselves a metropolis.
reading_mnemonic: In this metropolis everything is a toe (と). The someones are toes, walking around. The buildings are toes, too.

meaning_mnemonic: When something is heavy, you need a lot of power to move it. It’s not going to move unless you use a lot of power. That thing is heavy and unless you use all the power you got, it’s not moving.
reading_mnemonic: Remember that 1 ton weight? Well, actually it’s a doughnut (どう). A huge, massive, 1 ton doughnut. It’s super heavy and hard to move, but it’s delicious.

meaning_mnemonic: A standing mustache with legs is able to sell merchandise. Most mustaches can’t stand because they don’t have legs. This mustache, however, does. It also has a keen business sense, which is why it’s selling merchandise.
reading_mnemonic: The mustache is selling his merchandise so well that even the Shougun (しょう) notices. He leans down really close to the standing mustache man's merchandise and stays very still. Then he snaps his fingers and his servants come rushing out to buy it all!

meaning_mnemonic: In Asia they assume everyone's heart is automatically bad and evil.
reading_mnemonic: Luckily, people in Asia know how to get the evil badness out of your heart with acupuncture (あく).

meaning_mnemonic: If someone is headed in your direction with a gun, nock an arrow in your bow and gather your tribe behind you because it’s about to get real! This man with a gun is headed your direction and he doesn’t even know what you and your tribe are gonna do to him. If he gets any closer, you’re likely to shoot that arrow right at him.
reading_mnemonic: When he starts to get closer, you notice that this guy is a bosozoku (ぞく) bike gang member. Bosozoku means “running tribe” and this guy is running right at you. With a gun. So gather your own tribe behind you and prepare to defend yourself against this bosozoku member.

meaning_mnemonic: If a tsunami is higher than your forehead you better move those legs and find a tree to climb, because that thing is deep!
reading_mnemonic: You wait until the tsunami is only as deep as your shin (しん). Then you climb down the tree and wade home in the shin-deep water.
radical_breakdown: 氵|Tsunami, 冖|Forehead, 儿|Legs, 木|Tree

meaning_mnemonic: The king requests a sphere!
reading_mnemonic: The sphere is a cucumber (きゅう) sphere. A strange sphere shaped cucumber.

meaning_mnemonic: This building has easy access to sunshine. The sunlight shines right in, because it's a clear building.
reading_mnemonic: The sunshine gets into the building so easily, in fact, that it hits your yogurt (よう). The sunshine makes the yogurt... gross.

meaning_mnemonic: The roof, even though it's almost spring, is still covered in ice so it's cold. Inside the house is cold, outside the house is cold. Everything is cold!
reading_mnemonic: You can't stand the cold anymore, so you hire a samurai (さむ) to come try to hack the ice off of your roof with his sword. You stand outside shivering, and watching as the samurai tries to stab the ice off of your roof.

meaning_mnemonic: A criminal's heart will always be sad. No one chooses a life of crime if they're happy. And even if they seem like they're doing fine on the outside, deep down they're really sad.
reading_mnemonic: The sad feelings fill the criminal's body with heat (ひ). This heat spreads and radiates out. If you walk next to them on the street, you'll feel the sad heat floating by you.

meaning_mnemonic: A "crab moon" is a specific period of time.
reading_mnemonic: When the crab moon period of time is upon us, we must take a special key (き) and lock everything in such a way that crabs cannot get in.

meaning_mnemonic: Stop! That box of rice is actually full of teeth! I know it says "rice" on the cover, but I promise you those are all teeth and if you bite into them you'll break a tooth of your own.
reading_mnemonic: Why do I have a rice box full of teeth? Ha (は)! Wouldn't you like to know. Ha! I definitely have an answer that isn't weird or creepy. Ha... ha ha...

meaning_mnemonic: There's a tsunami coming and you want to be together with it by yourself (oneself) so you go to the harbor.
reading_mnemonic: As you look around at the harbor in your last moments you suddenly see someone in the water. It's こういち! He's sitting in an inner tube in the harbor waiting for the tsunami too.

meaning_mnemonic: There's a tent of beans. You try to climb it.
reading_mnemonic: You climb the bean tent, and from this vantage point you can see とうきょう in the distance.

meaning_mnemonic: A horned king on a slide catches your eye because you love what he's chosen to wear. You can't wait for him to arrive at the bottom of the slide so you can check out his outfit close-up.
reading_mnemonic: How does this king decide what to wear each day? He uses chalk (ちゃく) to sketch out his wardrobe ideas on a chalkboard. This helps him arrive at a conclusion faster.
radical_breakdown: 丷|Horns, 王|King, 丿|Slide, 目|Eye

meaning_mnemonic: The village beforehand (what the village was before it was a village) was a field.
reading_mnemonic: On this field, the Yankees (や) used to play.

meaning_mnemonic: The life radical and the life kanji are the same, so hopefully you now just know them both.
reading_mnemonic: You can save life or take it away with your new saber (せい). This is the saber you got from doing the correct thing (remember?), and now you need to figure out how to use it with this life. So what do you do?

meaning_mnemonic: The radical death and the kanji death are the same.
reading_mnemonic: Your death will be because of a bowling (ぼう) accident. Oh, you didn't know? You're going to be hit by a giant bowling ball and crushed flat.

meaning_mnemonic: The radical suit and the kanji suit are exactly the same! This kanji can also mean join which makes sense. When something suits you well, like a hat or something, it joins together with you quite well too. Join me, my hat! You suit my head well. It just fits, you know?
reading_mnemonic: You need someone who will suit you. Someone who can join you on your life journey. So you call Grandpa ごういち. Note: For the ごう reading mnemonics, we use Grandpa ごういち because こういち is used for the こう reading. So just remember that ごう comes from Koichi's grandpa ごういち.

meaning_mnemonic: You look at a table and notice it is being used as a slide by insects to launch themselves into the wind. This kanji can also mean style. To remember this, consider how styles can change quickly, just like the wind!
reading_mnemonic: You wonder what's pushing these insects to jump into the wind in such a manner, and you realize that it's because they've had way too much food (ふう).

meaning_mnemonic: What does your mama tell you to do in the street? Look before you cross! You gotta do it beforehand, or it could be too late.
reading_mnemonic: As you look beforehand, you see a yo-yo (よ) lying in the street.

meaning_mnemonic: Under a cliff there's a stool. If someone has a stool deep inside a cliff, they are most likely pretty anti-society, hiding away like that.
reading_mnemonic: Turns out, when you go to this guy and pull off his beard, its the anti-hero from Star Wars, Han (はん) Solo! What is Han doing here, so hidden away? He's obviously hiding from Jabba because he doesn't want to get frozen in carbonite again.

meaning_mnemonic: There's a standing tree that you're taking an axe to. You're going to cut down this tree to let a new tree grow.
reading_mnemonic: You cut down the tree to make room for a new one, but it falls on your shin (しん).

meaning_mnemonic: Your scooter is anti scoot. It doesn't want to run. So you have to return it.
reading_mnemonic: You return to the store and wait in line to return the scooter but the person working returns doesn't want you to return it. He stares you dead in the eyes, waves his hand, and turns you into a hen (へん)!

meaning_mnemonic: If you run into a gate mouth first, you’re going to have a problem. Smashing your mouth into a gate is going to hurt. A lot. The problem you’re now in is one of getting to a hospital and having your mouth sewn back on. The question is, how are you going to get to the hospital?
reading_mnemonic: The reason you ran mouth first into this gate was because you were being chased by a monster (もん). A monster in and of itself is a big enough problem as is, let alone smashing your mouth into a gate. You poor, hapless soul.

meaning_mnemonic: The roof under which the leader can house one hundred of his people is at the local lodge.
reading_mnemonic: The lodge shook (しゅく) as the hundred people came tumbling in through the door. It shook, but it didn't fall over. The roof stayed firmly in place, and everyone got to sleep under it okay.

meaning_mnemonic: Only a tree with eyes and a heart has the ability to imagine and to contemplate. For a tree to imagine and contemplate things, it needs eyes to see and a heart to feel.
reading_mnemonic: If a tree can imagine, it likely has a soul (そう). Its soul is what makes it possible for the tree to contemplate things, you see?

meaning_mnemonic: When a canine puts its mouth on your heart, it's a pretty unforgettable feeling.
reading_mnemonic: Overall, though, it's a good feeling — so good that you feel like Genghis Khan (かん)! With this canine lovingly slobbering on your heart, you feel like you could go out and conquer the world!

meaning_mnemonic: If the sun starts to make a sound, you know it's about to go dark. The sun isn't supposed to make a sound, so if you can hear it, it's probably about to fizzle out or something. After it's gone, obviously everything will be pitch black. Get ready to be in the dark!
reading_mnemonic: Now wandering around your house in the dark you start to feel hungry, so you reach blindly for some food and take a bite. Yuck! It's anchovies (あん). You don't even like anchovies, how did they get in your house? Hmm… Dark forces are at work here…

meaning_mnemonic: By a tree, there's a sheep in the water with a formal name ender. That means everyone calls him Sheep-sama. No one calls him just "Sheep," since he's kind of a big deal. He's actually like sheep royalty. When he's not in his castle, Sheep-sama enjoys playing in the water by the trees. This can also mean manner, as in your manner of doing things. I guess someone with a formal name ender has a different manner of doing things.
reading_mnemonic: This sheep with the formal name ender only likes to play outside in the water during the summer (さま). Summer is the best season for this fancy sheep. The other seasons just can't compare.

meaning_mnemonic: When a spirit decides to live in your scarecrow, you'll be granted good luck and good fortune. Crows won't hang out in your farm. Everything you grow will become large and delicious. But not everyone is so lucky that a spirit will decide to live in their scarecrow. So maybe the luck was in you all along!
reading_mnemonic: You want to check the scarecrow to make sure your recent luck is coming from it, so you kick it. "F*** (ふく) you!" it yells. Oh yeah, there's a spirit in there.

meaning_mnemonic: Gold, at its root, is made up of silver. Using silver as the root of a coin is a great way to save on gold! That's why, often, if you just scratch gold, you'll find there's silver hidden underneath, at its root.
reading_mnemonic: If you want to hunt for some silver for yourself, all you need is a guinea (ぎん) pig. Guinea pigs can smell silver, so get a couple and set them loose in the woods and they'll lead you straight to it.

meaning_mnemonic: The sun shines down on your coat rack to reveal your geoduck-patterned jacket, which then becomes the major topic of discussion all around town.
reading_mnemonic: After a few days, the topic changes from the cool geoduck design to what kind of dye (だい) you used to get those real-to-life geoduck colors.

meaning_mnemonic: Eating the roof is a bear, because the roof is a public building. Because it is a public building bears are allowed to eat the roof.
reading_mnemonic: Public buildings must make their roofs available for eating because of a law passed by Genghis Khan (かん).

meaning_mnemonic: A horse and a shrimp are sitting next to each other. They are both at the train station, waiting for a train to come and take them home.
reading_mnemonic: The train pulls into the station. They walk up to the train doors, but they don't open. "Perhaps a key (えき) would help?" asks the station master, as he goes over to open the door to the train.

meaning_mnemonic: You have a rice ladle that's specifically for paying the rice fee. Each scoop of something has an extra fee tacked on, so when you use a material, there's a fee you have to pay in that material as well.
reading_mnemonic: One day, the fee ladle is suddenly the size of row (りょう) boat oars! What! You're supposed to pay a row boat sized fee now?!

meaning_mnemonic: There's treasure in this tree so you take out your weapon and kill it.
reading_mnemonic: But after the kill, Satsuki (さつ) appears and yells at you. She likes trees — remember how she protected one in the 札 mnemonic? — so Satsuki's pretty upset you'd kill one like that.

meaning_mnemonic: Under a misshapen crescent moon, a dog boils as much nature as it can find.
reading_mnemonic: Destroying nature like this is the dog's way of practicing Zen (ぜん) Buddhism. As it breathes in the fumes from all of the different pieces of nature being boiled down, the dog gets really zen and chill.

meaning_mnemonic: Your womb spins in a circle and starts to boil with heat. Uh oh, I think you have a fever.
reading_mnemonic: The heat from your fever is making your insides and your head and your entire body spin and boil, until your doctor throws some nets (ねつ) around you. You were flailing around and they couldn't get you to stop, so they had to catch you in a series of nets.

meaning_mnemonic: The Viking opens his mouth, and below it, a shellfish sits. Grab that shellfish and throw it into his mouth to win a prize!
reading_mnemonic: The prize you're working so hard to win is lunch with the Shougun (しょう). This is a pretty huge prize, considering all you're doing is knocking something over.

meaning_mnemonic: You want to get a scooter, so you have one self (oneself) and another self working together to choose. The two tiny yous sit on each of your shoulders, like angel and devil, and argue about which scooter you should choose.
reading_mnemonic: Suddenly your selfs both gasp and choose a scooter in front of you that looks like a centaur (せん). The scooter is designed like a human on the top, the bars are its arms, and the bottom with the seat and the wheels are all horse. This centaur scooter is what you choose to ride.

meaning_mnemonic: The original geoduck had a request. He wants there to be more geoducks in the world!
reading_mnemonic: The only person that would even hear the geoduck's request was Gandhi (がん). Gandhi closed his eyes, sat down, and spread the geoduck's request to the rest of the world.

meaning_mnemonic: Your soul is blue. As in, it's sad and not feeling well. This is because your soul changes colors depending on your feelings or what emotions you're expressing.
reading_mnemonic: Why is your soul feeling blue? Because Joe (じょう), the big local farmhand, was extremely mean to you.

meaning_mnemonic: The sun in the center of the sky gives off its light, which reflects off of everything around it.
reading_mnemonic: This reflected light is important for acorns (えい), in particular. Without light reflecting off everything, the sun's light would never make it down to the ground where they've fallen. They would never grow into trees. And we'd all suffocate.

meaning_mnemonic: You reach for a spoon to start eating, but your mama hands you an arrow instead and points towards the coat rack. Hm, that's not like her… Suddenly you're filled with doubt. Is this really your mama? You doubt it.
reading_mnemonic: Now full of doubt, you decide to test your mama by putting her in a guillotine (ぎ). It sounds harsh, but the guillotine is the only way to clear up your doubts.
radical_breakdown: 匕|Spoon, マ|Mama, 矢|Arrow, 疋|Coat Rack

meaning_mnemonic: If you compare white light to the other colors you'll realize... white consists of all the colors in one. It contains all the colors in the spectrum in one color. It is the one color that is everything.
reading_mnemonic: You decide white light is the ultimate color. You decide you want to put it on all things to make everything white. "What a great idea," you think. You try to put it on everything and you nearly succeed... except, the miners (みな). They keep getting dirty doing all their mining things. NOOO, your plan is ruined!

meaning_mnemonic: The leader of the yakuza shows you his knife. He says, "This is an example of a knife."
reading_mnemonic: "This is an example," the leader of the yakuza tells you. "Next time, I'll show you an example of a ray (れい) gun."

meaning_mnemonic: Next to the cross we combine our power power power so that we have cooperation. And with our powers combined, we become stronger than we ever could have been apart, lifting the cross above our heads!
reading_mnemonic: Nowhere is the power of cooperation more apparent than in きょうと. When invaders are attacking, when the townspeople want to rebel, when there is a kitty up a tree, the people combine their power from all reaches of Japan and cross into きょうと to put a stop to the madness through cooperation.

meaning_mnemonic: You try to be private, but because of your big hair you end up having to participate in everything. Can you imagine people asking for volunteers or something, and you trying to look inconspicuous with your big hair? Of course they're going to notice you and make you participate.
reading_mnemonic: You know who has big hair and loves to participate in everything? Santa-san (さん)! Well, his hair is more big on the bottom (it's a beard) than whatever you have on your head, but hair is hair. And he participates in present-giving in every house in the world! See? Big hair = participation!

meaning_mnemonic: The roof that became the origin of all roofs was perfect. It was tall and wide so it could fit and protect everyone. And the dimensions were perfect too.
reading_mnemonic: This perfect roof was commissioned by Genghis Khan (かん). We got all of the carpenters and home makers and construction workers he'd conquered together and tasked them with making the first roof, but only if they made it absolutely perfect.

meaning_mnemonic: If you live in the now, there’s a good chance your heart controls your thought process. You don’t have time to think with your brain, you need an answer now so you use your heart to make decisions and thought process.
reading_mnemonic: You're living in the now and letting your heart control all your thoughts. Why are you following your heart? You found you only have one 年 (ねん) to live, so you have to live for the now.

meaning_mnemonic: If your fingers are strong enough, you can take an axe and fold it in half. But be careful not to bend it too far, or you might just break it!
reading_mnemonic: Unfortunately, as you fold these axes in half you realize they come in sets (せつ), so there are twice the axes you thought there would be. To compensate, you start folding them in sets too.

meaning_mnemonic: Causing death at every turn, the moon king sits inside his moon, getting ready to cause death on anything in his sights. Sounds a lot like the Death Star from a certain movie. One of which is "Star Wars: A New Hope."
reading_mnemonic: The name A New Hope, as we all know, comes from the ending where the moon king's son sends a bowling (ぼう) ball into that little opening and knocks it out of the sky.

meaning_mnemonic: The bundle radical and the bundle kanji are the same!
reading_mnemonic: You should always bundle your socks (そく). If you don't, there is a 100% chance you'll lose all of the left ones.

meaning_mnemonic: Yakuza bars barely exist. The remainder of them aren't even in Japan.
reading_mnemonic: The remainder of the yakuza bars aren't in Japan. Strangely, they are all in Zanzibar (ざん).

meaning_mnemonic: Look at the ground! You spilled some water drops, so I request that you wipe them up. I'd do it myself, but you're the one who spilled them, so I'm requesting that you do it. Pretty reasonable request, right?
reading_mnemonic: Oh, one more thing. I request that you wipe up the water with this cucumber (きゅう).

meaning_mnemonic: You tie a thread on your finger before jumping in the pool to remind yourself of the promise you made to your mother. The thread represents the promise you made to mow the lawn after you finished swimming in the pool.
reading_mnemonic: After you get out of the pool, you keep the promise you made to your mother. So you get on your yak (やく) powered mower and trim the grass. Yes, your mower is pulled by a yak. It’s very efficient.

meaning_mnemonic: Everyone has a soul in their life, and that soul shapes their gender. It's not just about body parts — it's about what's inside. In the end, it's one's nature that truly matters.
reading_mnemonic: Once you've decided what your gender is, someone comes to your house and lays a saber (せい) on your shoulders. "This is now your nature," they say, lifting the saber. It's official! It's in all the newspapers, there's a parade, and everyone pats you on the back. Thanks, gender saber!

meaning_mnemonic: You can make your fingers branch out. It's your special skill, a very advanced technique. Your fingers branch out into smaller fingers and you can hold things really well. You can type super-duper fast. And you can win any tickle fight. These are skills you have thanks to your branching fingers.
reading_mnemonic: Unfortunately, these skills are too much for the normal skill-less people to handle, so they pull out the guillotine (ぎ). I guess they're going to chop off your skillful fingers because they're kinda scary.

meaning_mnemonic: If a tree wants to kiss you, it's a sign of your status. Only someone of high status would be worthy enough to receive the gnarly but gentle kiss of a tree. Trees don't kiss just anyone, you know.
reading_mnemonic: The best way to convince a tree of your status is to say "cock-a-doodle-doo" at it, like a cock (かく), i.e. a male chicken. Trees really place a lot of status on the ability to sound like a cock crowing.

meaning_mnemonic: In a private place on the moon, you hide two spoons that give you a special ability. It's the ability to predict the future! The private moon spoons reflect the knowledge of time and space into your brain. Now that's a cool ability!
reading_mnemonic: This ability to predict the future makes you famous and now everyone knows your name: Nostradamus (のう)! And now that people know about your name and special ability, everyone will love you!

meaning_mnemonic: There go some angels with drops on their shoulders. Carrying drops like that requires technique. It’s a real art.
reading_mnemonic: Angels are so good at this because they are trained in ninjutsu (じゅつ), or the "ninja techniques." Everyone knows that ninjas are great at carrying drops on the go!

meaning_mnemonic: Your private grains are meant to stay private! You shouldn't be sharing them with the whole town, they're just for you. This kanji also means I. Why? Because what's more private than you? I mean, I! Basically, some things are only the business of you (I) and those things should be private.
reading_mnemonic: You're getting into the zone, thinking about yourself (I) and how much you love having things that are private and just yours, when you realize there is a sheep (し) in this grain bag. And it's eating all of your (I's) private grains. No!

meaning_mnemonic: You pick up your knife and broom because you're getting ready to return home. There'll be a lot of work to do when you return home — cooking, cleaning, fixing stuff — so your knife and broom are sure to come in handy.
reading_mnemonic: For you to return home, your family has to ask the world to 返す (かえ) you to them. You belong at home with your family — the outside world is just borrowing you, and eventually it needs to 返す you and let you return home.

meaning_mnemonic: When you see the spring sun you know it's finally the spring season.
reading_mnemonic: When the spring season comes around, it makes you want to laugh: "HAR (はる) HAR HAR!" you yell.

meaning_mnemonic: A giant shrimp appears on top of the sun after it rises high above the ground, and this is how you know it's noon. The shrimp appears on the sun exactly at noon every day, to announce that it's noon.
reading_mnemonic: At noon, the shrimp also puts on its high heels (ひる). It wants to look good for the other shrimp it's going to lunch with. High noon? More like high heels, am I right?

meaning_mnemonic: The sun is out, the sky is blue, things have begun to clear up!
reading_mnemonic: Now that it's starting to clear up you can't help but laugh. "Ha (は)! Ha ha ha!" you laugh up into the sky. The sun feels great on your face, making you feel lively! And that blue sky ain't too shabby either.

meaning_mnemonic: Grains look like they're on fire in autumn. They all turn red and orange and brown, the colors of fire. It's also fun to set grains on fire in Autumn, since it's getting colder.
reading_mnemonic: As the grains burn, and the season changes to autumn, imagine them yelling out in pain: "ACK (あき)!"

meaning_mnemonic: If you want to say how big a cross is, you have to measure it. You can't say the size of something without measuring it first.
reading_mnemonic: You need to measure this cross but all you have is a cake (けい). Good enough! I'm sure all cakes are exactly the same size, so they're a reliable unit of measure.

meaning_mnemonic: Take your yakuza knife and put it in a row with the others.
reading_mnemonic: Should we put them in a row? Let's (れつ) put them in a row!

meaning_mnemonic: This cage with treasure in it is actually a map of the district the treasure is in.
reading_mnemonic: There is one district you're interested in, and that's the cookie (く) district.

meaning_mnemonic: A good ceremony is under construction for a long time. You can't just make up a new ceremony on the spot. A ceremony is done a certain way because that's the way it's always been done. In short, to build a ceremony, you have to create a ritual first. Then, the ritual can be constructed into a bigger, more lavish ceremony. This kanji also means equation for some reason. Just think of a ceremony that involves doing math and solving equations. How strange would that be? Pretend you're at this ceremony.
reading_mnemonic: So, you're at a ritual, but not just any old ritual. This is a full-blown ceremony and it's incredibly chic (しき). Imagine just how chic it is. Give it a shot — I'll let you come up with the chicness this time (it's good practice).

meaning_mnemonic: To your leader, you say: "Believe and trust in me." The leader doesn't think you can handle your duties, so you have to say this to him. You want him to believe and trust that you're responsible. You can handle this task.
reading_mnemonic: As you face your leader and say "Believe and trust in me," you kneel down on each shin (しん). You have shin splints, so it hurts a bit, but you do it anyway to show how serious you are.

meaning_mnemonic: The simple radical and the simple kanji are the same!
reading_mnemonic: One of the most simple things in the world is getting a tan (たん). All you have to do is stand outside long enough. It doesn't matter what skin type you have or what the weather is like. Eventually, if you stand out there long enough, you'll get a tan.

meaning_mnemonic: Again and again, winter changes you each year.
reading_mnemonic: You know what else changes each winter? Hens (へん)! They're constantly laying eggs, which then (possibly) turn into new hens.

meaning_mnemonic: The husband radical and the husband kanji are the same. How useful, unlike some husbands, I'd imagine.
reading_mnemonic: What do all husbands love? Food (ふう)! Can you hear your future husband? He’s saying, "Fooooood! FOOOOOD!” like some kind of food craving zombie.

meaning_mnemonic: Your magic yoga brush lets you build what's in your mind's eye.
reading_mnemonic: You build a bridge. Immediately after, someone is climbing up onto it. It's Ken (けん) the samurai. He waves at you and says, "Did you build this? The craftsmanship is amazing."

meaning_mnemonic: Once the sun comes out, you can use this key to unlock it and take you to any previous day, even just yesterday! The sun is in charge of the day changes, so if you use a key to unlock it, you can control the flow of time and return to yesterday, or a previous day in the past. Behold the power of the sun.
reading_mnemonic: Time traveling to a previous time, like yesterday, can be rough on the body. As such, you wear a small sack (さく) to hold your valuables while you're ripped through the sands of time. The sack keeps your important stuff from getting lost. The sack holds your key to the sun as well.

meaning_mnemonic: Tsunamis in the past changed the methods and laws of today.
reading_mnemonic: These methods and laws affected your own home (ほう) the most.

meaning_mnemonic: There are many flowers in the center of England. It may seem rainy and gray at first, but if you walk right to the center you'll see all the flowers that grow there in the center of the country. This kanji also means English, which is pretty similar to England. Just imagine all the people of England walking to the center, where the flowers are, and speaking English to them to help them grow.
reading_mnemonic: You keep walking to the very central center of England and see a giant acorn (えい) planted in the middle of the ground. This acorn is the source of all the flowers and life in England.

meaning_mnemonic: You run into someone's forehead with your car. The big forehead you hit is Kim Jong Un's. You know that now you're going to have the whole North Korean army coming after you.
reading_mnemonic: The army is after you. Each army soldier has a gun (ぐん) and they want to use these guns of theirs to shoot you dead! You killed their leader with a car and now they’re gonna get you back with a gun!

meaning_mnemonic: You might want to eat, but your anti-eating stance means your meal will just sit in front of you, uneaten. Food is meant to be eaten! Stop trying to fast and take a bite.
reading_mnemonic: As you stare at the meal, Han (はん) Solo appears before you and takes a bite! This is what happens if you don't eat your food, someone else will eat it.

meaning_mnemonic: The sun has an excuse for disappearing at night. The sun gets really tired, same as anyone else – so when night rolls around the sun excuses itself and goes to sleep. It’s a valid excuse.
reading_mnemonic: Unfortunately, you also have a history of overworking yourself, so you've been outright banned (ばん) from showing up at night.

meaning_mnemonic: If you see an animal among the flowers in a rice paddy, chances are it’s a cat. Cats love rice paddy flowers, almost as much as they love catnip.
reading_mnemonic: Wait a minute… This cat is pretty odd looking. You take a closer look, seeing it is missing its neck (ねこ). You go to pet it, but it's super sensitive about that area of its head, which is basically a face connected to a body...

meaning_mnemonic: You examine the mouth of a zombie and find a small garden in there. There are even benches... it looks like a park.
reading_mnemonic: You look closer at the garden and suddenly everything ends (えん).

meaning_mnemonic: When the sun is out, you can see two Wolverines and a turkey playing together, but only on a certain weekday. Which day of the week is it? I'll never tell you. It could be Sunday. It could be Monday. It could be any day of the week.
