reading_mnemonic: Now that you know how to figure out what day of the week it is, you can start making yogurt (よう). It can take up to 24 hours to make yogurt. Knowing which weekday it is at any given moment means you can perfect your yogurt-making schedule.

meaning_mnemonic: Why would you try to take a brush to the sun? It's almost too obvious, because you want to write something down.
reading_mnemonic: What did you write about? You were writing about this amazing circus show (しょ) you just watched on the sun. You didn't expect there to be any shows here, but turns out you were wrong!

meaning_mnemonic: You see a scooter with a zombie on it, going really far away. Someone tied that zombie to the scooter and now it's far off in the distance, groaning and growling.
reading_mnemonic: The zombie goes so far, that its life ends (えん). Zombies need to eat to live (it's really all they need), but they go so far on their scooter trip, that they just give up and end it all.

meaning_mnemonic: A psychic leader kneels to the ground, picks up a thread, and instantly makes a connection with the person that it came from. This leader is very powerful, so even a thread is enough for them to make a psychic connection with the person who was wearing it.
reading_mnemonic: As you develop this psychic connection with the owner of the thread, you can tell that they're currently eating a cake (けい).

meaning_mnemonic: There's an ear just sitting on a stool. Nobody's watching, so, you take it.
reading_mnemonic: You're the kind of person who likes to take things. "What things?" you ask. Little toes (と). Because that isn't creepy.

meaning_mnemonic: The kanji is the same as the products radical, so it means product — you know, the kind of articles or goods you buy and sell.
reading_mnemonic: As you try to sell some products, you finally get a buyer. It's a Hindu (ひん) person. She walks in and buys your products on the spot!

meaning_mnemonic: Your roof needs measurements done every year to make sure it will protect you properly.
reading_mnemonic: If the measurements are off, and your roof doesn't protect you, then you get to sue (す)! If you're still alive, that is.

meaning_mnemonic: Put a lid on something spicy and you'll cook up pure happiness.
reading_mnemonic: Out of spicy foods you made pure happiness. You give it to your sad friend こういち, who waits at the table.

meaning_mnemonic: In the prison where you once kept Wolverine, you find a beating heart. You don't understand how it's still going, but you know you need to hurry up and do something, or it might stop all of a sudden.
reading_mnemonic: You start to overheat as you hurry around, so you grab a cucumber (きゅう) to cool you down. The high water content re-hydrates you and lets you continue hurrying to help save this heart.

meaning_mnemonic: If the pope stays fixated on the ground, staring at fins, he's going to lose touch with reality. He should be focusing on his popish duties, but instead he's looking at the fish fins he dropped, and now can't eat because they're dirty. Silly pope. You can't let this one thing get you down. You have other things to do.
reading_mnemonic: You're doing your best to bring the pope back to reality when he snaps and kicks you in the shin (しん). Oww! What the heck, pope! But he's already back staring at the fins and your shin is throbbing where he kicked it.

meaning_mnemonic: With the bamboo from that tree, your trained eye can tell it'll make an excellent box. Boxes made from bamboo trees are very sturdy and fashionable. You have an eye for fashion as well, you see.
reading_mnemonic: Now you can use that box to store all your hardcore (はこ) punk vinyl records. You're a real connoisseur, so you know that hardcore music should only ever be kept in bamboo boxes.

meaning_mnemonic: The face radical and the face kanji are the same! But this isn't just a face like the one you're looking at your computer/phone with. It's the surface kind of face too!
reading_mnemonic: This face you're looking at, that has a lot of surface area, belongs to men (めん). Not a single man, but all men put together. It's hundreds of thousands of men's faces in a row.

meaning_mnemonic: If there is a drum in your mouth it's time to rejoice! And because of your mouth drum your rejoicing will be loud and booming!
reading_mnemonic: You loudly rejoice for a while when suddenly someone runs over and shoves a key (き) in your mouth, locking it shut. You can't rejoice anymore! You need that key to unlock your mouth!

meaning_mnemonic: A canopy attaching your entire country is the government. They loom over you all and try to keep you all organized and together under their control.
reading_mnemonic: Try to get out from under this government canopy and you'll be labeled a fool (ふ). Unless... you can fool them!

meaning_mnemonic: After a tsunami, use this machine to cure the people and the country from the damage. Healing machines are all over Japan just in case a tsunami does way more damage than they can handle. Oh, and whoever cures and heals the most people will be able to rule over them once everything starts going back to normal. So keep that in mind, kay?
reading_mnemonic: Alternative ways to cure yourself after a tsunami are either praying to Jesus (じ) or eating your weight in cheese (ち). I'm not sure if I have enough cheese for all the people that got hit though... Hmm, do you have cheese? Before you make your decision, remember that whoever cures you will be able to reign over you and your people. So do you want to be led by Jesus or by some cheese? The choice is yours.

meaning_mnemonic: Bamboo heaven is a place for laughing. Bamboo is a very jolly plant, and they love to laugh. Even after death in bamboo heaven, the bamboo continue to laugh joyfully. Bamboo heaven is truly a place of laughter.
reading_mnemonic: There’s actually a war a goin’ on up in that there bamboo heaven, y’know? Ye might not have heard of it with all that there laughin’ a goin’ on, but there definitely be a war a (わら) goin’ on up in bamboo heaven, y’hear? The bamboo are scared so that’s why they be laughin’ so much. They nervous.

meaning_mnemonic: When your tongue becomes too spicy for you to bear, it’s time to quit the jalapeño eating contest. You’ve been eating them for three hours now and the spiciness from the peppers is really burning your tongue. Throw in the towel, it’s time to quit the contest. This kanji has another meaning too: Eating isn't the only thing that makes your tongue spicy, so do certain words. Say your favorite words out loud right now. Feel them on your tongue. Words are the spicy food of language!
reading_mnemonic: Oh, you're probably wondering who won that spicy food contest after you quit and became obsessed with words instead. It was Jesus (じ). Who did you expect? He was great with words AND never quitting when things got spicy.

meaning_mnemonic: This gate of horns will take you to heaven. These horns are related and connected to heaven in some way.
reading_mnemonic: They are related and connected to heaven because these are the horns that Genghis Khan (かん) made from his enemies. God said he could come into heaven if he made a gate of horns, so that's what he did.

meaning_mnemonic: It's correct in winter to focus on politics and the government. Elections are happening, in the new year politicians are being sworn in. Winter is government time!
reading_mnemonic: Everyone involved in politics and government wields a special saber (せい). If two political parties are arguing, they'll whip out their sabers and start slashing away!

meaning_mnemonic: A group of private sword guys are in your rice paddy. You must detain them at once! Private sword guys are people who work for private companies and use their swords on people. They're basically paid assassins. And you're going to detain them!
reading_mnemonic: You're running out of steam and you're afraid you might not be able to detain all of these guys when Ryu (りゅう) from Street Fighter appears. He hates swords, and will only use fists because it's the honorable way to fight, so he starts helping you detain them! He's also found a loophole (る) in the system and you don't have to be super gentle with these guys either. So detain them as forcefully as you want. It is your rice paddy they're in, after all.

meaning_mnemonic: Going into a building made by a squid is risky. First of all, squids only have tentacles, no bones, and they make all of their buildings out of risky materials like kelp and sharp coral.
reading_mnemonic: "It's too risky, leave me!" the squid cries. "I'll save you, underwater citizen! Nothing is too risky for Ken (けん) the samurai!" The building is collapsing on the squid, the risk is so great, but Ken the samurai dives in and saves him!

meaning_mnemonic: There is a prison on a cliff surrounded by snakes. Now that's a dangerous place. If you try to escape the prison you either fall to your death off the cliff or get bitten/squeezed to death by the snakes. Can you think of anything more dangerous than this? I can't.
reading_mnemonic: Lucky for you, even though you're stuck in this dangerous place, there is hope. There is a key (き). All dangerous prisons have a key. You just have to find and steal it so you can avoid the cliffs and snakes!

meaning_mnemonic: If a narwhal sticks a child with its horn then you have to admit that it exists. We know some of you have been doubting narwhals and whether they're real. Well now your kid is a kabob, so do you believe they exist now? I suppose you do.
reading_mnemonic: Oh, and the child we had to narwhal stab to prove they exist - that's your son (そん). Maybe you should have listened and kept your son out of the Narwhal Danger Zone (ぞん) after we warned you about it.

meaning_mnemonic: The original radical and the original kanji are the same! This kanji can also mean field, probably because that's what everything originally looked like before humans: just a bunch of fields.
reading_mnemonic: The original Japanese hero was Genji (げん), from "The Tale of Genji."

meaning_mnemonic: Flowers can be used for comfort, but also for medicine. Sure, it’s a comfort to smell flowers because they smell nice, but one can also use them as medicine to heal people.
reading_mnemonic: The best way to transport all the medicine on land is with a yak (やく). Yaks are big, strong, and very capable of transporting flower medicine like these.

meaning_mnemonic: The leader of the shellfish has a knife in its side. It's fine though, don't worry, it's just a reminder that he won the great shellfish war back when they were trying to choose the new leader.
reading_mnemonic: Because of this knife in his side, he can't pronounce certain words correctly. The most obvious one is when he says 川 (かわ), but it comes out of the side of his mouth as がわ.

meaning_mnemonic: A Viking will empty his mouth of all its dirt in the great hall. They all get together in some kind of public chamber and dish all the dirt (literal and figurative) that they've got.
reading_mnemonic: While the Vikings gather to spill the dirt in their hall, they also stuff their faces with doughnuts (どう). Ah yes, Vikings love to eat doughnuts when they talk trash.

meaning_mnemonic: In a yurt you use a towel as a seat.
reading_mnemonic: Something about using a towel for a seat is very sexy (せき) to you. Probably because you associate it with sexy people using towel seats on the beach.

meaning_mnemonic: A shellfish that can't live through winter is a failure. Any proper shellfish would survive through the winter, so this is quite an embarrassing defeat.
reading_mnemonic: The best way to avoid failure is to say a little haiku (はい) to distract you from the cold. In fact, this can work in any situation where you're afraid of defeat. Say a haiku aloud, it will calm your nerves and warm you from the inside.

meaning_mnemonic: The fruit radical and the fruit kanji are exactly the same! Bodacious!
reading_mnemonic: They sell fruit at the store, and you need to drive your car (か) to get there. A car is the fastest way to fruit.

meaning_mnemonic: Your mouth is so big that it's the cause of all your problems.
reading_mnemonic: Your big mouth is the cause behind all your friends and family moving to an inn (いん). They move to the inn so they don't have to live with you and hear you talk anymore.

meaning_mnemonic: A viking with a mouth towel is a totally normal thing. It's ordinary.
reading_mnemonic: It's normal for a viking to have a mouth towel, but your sloppy farmhand friend Joe(じょう) has a mouth towel too. That's a habit that's only normal for vikings, so why does he have one?

meaning_mnemonic: If you can say what sound a drunkard makes, you must be very discerning. Few people are able to discern what sound a drunkard makes, but you — you can say, because you're a very discriminating listener.
reading_mnemonic: Discerning individuals like you are considered chic (しき). What's more chic than your discriminating way of listening?

meaning_mnemonic: A criminal has done an injustice on the world or other people. Being a criminal is a negative thing, and even if it was just a mistake, it was still a crime.
reading_mnemonic: When you commit an injustice, you'll know because heat (ひ) fills your body. Maybe you've never done any kind of big thing, but when you make a mistake your face fills with heat and you turn red!

meaning_mnemonic: Under this roof is a bear who works for the government. If you saw a bear out in the wild you might be afraid and try to run, but if you see a bear inside a building under a roof, don't be scared! It's just a government bear.
reading_mnemonic: The first government that allowed bears was set up by Genghis Khan (かん). He was all about conquering people and then using them as efficiently as possible. He discovered that bears are incredibly useful in government buildings as government workers.

meaning_mnemonic: If you're on the roof of the festival you'll have to guess what's actually going on below you. You can kind of see that there are rides and maybe food? It smells like food. But you have to guess on the specifics because you're above it and not in it.
reading_mnemonic: To get a better guess, you ask Satsuki (さつ) for help. She's that little girl you know from some earlier mnemonics, and she happens to be up on the roof with you. Picture her as you ask, "What's your guess, Satsuki?"

meaning_mnemonic: Put on cleats so you can plant a kiss on your sweetheart's forehead in the heart of winter — that's love. You'll be braving the harsh winter elements for love, so you put on your cleats to get a better grip on the snow. Sure, you could just wait for better weather to go see them, but then it wouldn't be true love, would it?
reading_mnemonic: Walking through the winter snow with your cleats on, you've gotta keep your eye (あい) on the prize. It's a really hard journey, but you keep your eye on the prize, which is your love and the time you'll get to spend with them.

meaning_mnemonic: You have a poem about winter that you say to warn people against going outside. It's cold and dangerous in winter! You admonish anyone and everyone you see going out there with your scary winter poem.
reading_mnemonic: To make sure people listen to your warning, you threaten to take away their cake (けい). People will do anything for cake, so when you bring it up, they actually take your attempts to warn them about winter seriously.

meaning_mnemonic: Viking see, Viking memorize. That’s how Vikings learn things. They see something, and then they memorize it. Quite simple, really. It can also mean awake. Just remember that Vikings can't see if they aren't awake. There won't be anything to memorize if their eyes are still closed, after all!
reading_mnemonic: Every morning, a cock (かく) crows and rouses the Vikings. Seeing this, one of the Vikings memorizes the cock crow so that he can mimic it and play pranks on his fellow Vikings.

meaning_mnemonic: What do you say to a guard? Your theory about how the thing he's guarding isn't even real. Yeah, you have this whole thing figured out. You have for a while. At this point, it's only fair that you tell your theory to the guard who's wasting his time.
reading_mnemonic: The guard listens to your theory but then he says his OWN! He thinks there are two sets (せつ) of guarded items, and he's only guarding one. According to his theory, either one could be real! His theory is more plausible, don't you think?

meaning_mnemonic: If you want to say something at a ceremony for construction workers you're going to have to try really hard. Construction is loud, so if you want to be heard you have to attempt to be louder than the drilling and smashing and digging and handing out of awards.
reading_mnemonic: You try to get their attention the only way you know how, by lifting a sheep (し) above your head. The sheep baas and suddenly everything is silent, all eyes are on you. Well, they're on the sheep.

meaning_mnemonic: You see a slide covered in dirt and use your mouth to clean it off. Then, you announce to everyone that the slide is clean and they can use it safely again.
reading_mnemonic: After you announce the slide is clean, you take a big swig of Coke (こく). The dirty slide left a nasty taste in your mouth, but the Coke is helping to wash it away.

meaning_mnemonic: If a grain seems extra heavy, you know it's a different kind. Not all types of grains are the same. So when you feel the heavy type, you know it isn't the same as the light kind.
reading_mnemonic: You sort all of the different kinds and types by putting them in the right chutes (しゅ). They slide away, probably to some big type-based piles you can't see.

meaning_mnemonic: You ride your scooter through the dirt while carrying a sheep because you're determined to attain something. Greatness? Glory? Everlasting fame? Maybe you'll attain a plural combination of all those things. After all, you are the best sheep-carrying off-road scooterist the world has ever seen.
reading_mnemonic: After you attain that plural combination of glory, greatness, and fame, you get a tattoo (たつ) to celebrate: "world's greatest," in gothic lettering, above a picture of you and your sheep on your scooter.

meaning_mnemonic: The rice you feed to a big geoduck can be of any type, kind, or category. It doesn't matter what kind of rice it is, the big geoduck will eat it.
reading_mnemonic: While eating every type and kind of rice from every category, the big geoduck has become even bigger. Its body is ruined (るい). It's painfully obese. This geoduck has eaten itself to ruin.

meaning_mnemonic: You want to share happiness with people so you stamp stools with the news. Now when people want a report of all the happy things going on, they can just look down before they sit.
reading_mnemonic: You research and report the news from home (ほう). Only after, once all of the news is stamped onto the stools, do you leave your home.

meaning_mnemonic: The bamboo temple is equal to all of the other non-bamboo temples. Just because it's made of bamboo doesn't make it any less special and spiritual.
reading_mnemonic: The bamboo temple is also an equal distance away from the other temples in とうきょう. When you look at a map of とうきょう temples, you can measure them out and they'll all be perfectly equal.

meaning_mnemonic: Your leader from long ago thought to borrow something precious from you. This leader did not return the thing he borrowed, and now he will pay.
reading_mnemonic: In your rage, you decide to find this leader, take back what's yours, and in return, borrow the leader's life. So you found him, grabbed him, and threw him into a shack (しゃく) — where you "borrow" a few parts of the leader himself, and do other terrible things to him.

meaning_mnemonic: Under a canopy, there are two persons on the dirt. What do they do there? They sit. The people use the dirt under the canopy as a seat for their butts.
reading_mnemonic: Who decided people have to sit like this? The Czar (ざ). The Czar wants to be above everyone, so he makes them sit on the dirt under canopies while he goes around on horseback or something, towering over them as they sit.

meaning_mnemonic: The death of your heart will cause you to forget all of the most important things. People think memories are kept in your brain, but that's not true. Your heart is where all of your most precious memories are kept, and when it dies, you forget them all.
reading_mnemonic: When someone forgets everything they're left with only one thing to do: go bowling (ぼう). Bowling is easy, and there's nothing to forget. You pick up a ball. You drop it. Everything else is automatically taken care of.

meaning_mnemonic: A tsunami previously gave everything in this town a good wash. There are many laundromats in this town, so when the previous tsunami hit, all of the detergent mixed with the water and gave everything a good wash.
reading_mnemonic: It wasn't just the town that got a wash, it was the centaurs (せん) too. (Centaurs happen to live in this town.) And being half horse, centaurs have a lot of hair that needs washing. Luckily, the soap tsunami gave them a good wash too.

meaning_mnemonic: A horse and a squid are going to test you.
reading_mnemonic: The test is being supervised by Ken (けん) the samurai.

meaning_mnemonic: Say it at noon. That's the only time I will allow you to say it. That's the only time I will permit you to say it. Other than that, no saying anything. Noon is your window.
reading_mnemonic: Where do these archaic horrible rules exist? The smaller version of Kyoto, Little Kyoto (きょ). Normal Kyoto is just fine. This smaller one is where a group of people went to create their own little town with their own dumb rules.

meaning_mnemonic: Within the blue water, a conflict stirs, but is made quiet by the muffling power of liquid. Under this blue water is a great conflict between two sea monsters, but on the surface it appears peaceful and quiet as the water prevents sound from rising above the surface.
reading_mnemonic: As you watch below the quiet water, every once in a while a saber (せい) breaches the surface and quietly slices back down.

meaning_mnemonic: If you have a fire and a helicopter hovering beside it, there's going to be a lot of dirt and smoke billowing around. Mostly smoke, on account of the fire. Now it's in your eyes and mouth. It gets in your lungs and you can't breathe. Why, helicopter, why!
reading_mnemonic: The smoke is too much and you realize this is the end (えん) for you. You're gonna die here!

meaning_mnemonic: The power of your mouth lets you add words together to form a sentence. Marvel at the mighty additive power your mouth holds! You add words together in an amazing fashion!
reading_mnemonic: Your parents are so proud of you being able to add words together that they surprise you with a new car (か). Wow! You add some stickers to your bumper and add your favorite playlist to the car radio. Let's drive.

meaning_mnemonic: Direct a tsunami into a canine's mouth to decrease the amount of water that strikes the surrounding area.
reading_mnemonic: After you and your canine decrease the tsunami's power, Genji (げん) comes out to thank you. That tsunami was on track to wash away Genji's house, which would have forced him to majorly decrease his frivolous playboy activities.

meaning_mnemonic: If you put a roof over a valley it will change its form. Its appearance will alter completely!
reading_mnemonic: Its new appearance looks familiar to you, like it's a big yogurt (よう) cup! A valley with a roof on it looks exactly like a yogurt cup. Huh!

meaning_mnemonic: The easy radical and the easy kanji are the same!
reading_mnemonic: What would be an easy reading for this kanji? い! The sound easy starts with!

meaning_mnemonic: Give some shellfish to a talented person and they'll have no problem accumulating wealth. People with talent can make money out of pretty much anything, so shellfish are like easy-mode.
reading_mnemonic: This talented person really starts accumulating wealth when their cyborg (さい) is unveiled. It's a half-man, half-shellfish cyborg that plays the xylophone (ざい), and everyone wants to buy it.

meaning_mnemonic: There are flowers on your right to show that you're still young. Your body still works, you're happy, you have your entire life ahead of you! And everything smells like flowers.
reading_mnemonic: When young people look to the right, they'll see their future: a walker (わか). You know, those metal contraptions with tennis balls on the bottoms to make sure they don't scrape the floor. Everything may be flowers and happiness now, but your future is in a walker.

meaning_mnemonic: You'll work your soul to death if you're too busy. Being busy just isn't good for your soul. Take breaks. Go on vacation. Don't be so busy that you destroy yourself.
reading_mnemonic: Take time out of your busy life and go bowling (ぼう) once in a while. In fact, you should probably go bowling once a week at least. Nothing brings energy back to your life like some relaxing bowling.

meaning_mnemonic: Use your mouth to take a measurement of this group. Just stretch your mouth out and around every single person. Get 'em all in there.
reading_mnemonic: This group is so big it takes you till dawn (だん) to get your measurement: they weigh a ton (とん) too!

meaning_mnemonic: “Don’t loiter – run, Junior!” said Indiana Jones Senior to Indiana Jones Junior. They’re escaping from a sticky situation and Junior was just loitering around like a fool. It’s no time to loiter, it’s time to run!
reading_mnemonic: Deciding not to loiter any longer, Indiana Jones Junior takes his dad’s advice and starts to run. Unfortunately he wasn’t paying attention to where his feet were and he stubbed his toe (と) on a jagged rock. His toe is in so much pain that he can’t bear to run any longer.

meaning_mnemonic: If you loiter around the sun temple, it's likely you'll acquire something. When you loiter around like that it looks like you're waiting for something, so if someone puts something in your hands and you just happen to acquire it, well, no one can fault you for that.
reading_mnemonic: You managed to acquire some tobacco, but just as you're about to leave Tokugawa (とく) Ieyasu comes marching up to you!! Or at least, his ghost does. He stares you dead in the eyes and says, "I didn't found the shogunate for you to acquire illegal goods and kill your body toking on my soil."

meaning_mnemonic: It's important to focus oneself in winter so that one can emerge renewed! You can't really go outside in winter without getting cold or sick, so spend winter focusing on YOU.
reading_mnemonic: Winter ends and, renewed, you come out ready to start a new hobby: kayaking (かい)! Nothing says renewal like a brand new kayak and sense of purpose in life.

meaning_mnemonic: You have to gather thread to sell if you want to continue living. You want to make a living, don't you? Make sure you continue to sell that thread every single day!
reading_mnemonic: You have to continue to sell that thread because a Bosozoku (ぞく) bike gang is forcing you to do it. You see? If you want to continue to live, you have to appease this Bosozoku gang. You better keep selling!

meaning_mnemonic: Your scooter and your car is what you always take along with you. Make sure they're connected well so you don't lose them!
reading_mnemonic: You take along your scooter and your car. Anything else, you can do a rental (れん) for!

meaning_mnemonic: If you put your mouth on a tree and try to eat it, you’re probably a distressed and troubled individual (unless you’re a woodchuck). You don’t need to eat this tree, you have plenty of food at home. Get your mouth off that tree you distressed child.
reading_mnemonic: You thought you were the most distressed and troubled person in this situation, but then you look up and see a very equally distressed and troubled condor (こん). The tree you've been mouthing is its home. And now you've slobbered all over it, ruining this condor's day.

meaning_mnemonic: The compare radical and the compare kanji are exactly the same! Huzzah!
reading_mnemonic: Compare the heat (ひ) today with the heat yesterday. Is it hotter today? It's up to you to compare.

meaning_mnemonic: Next to a tree, you spot poop, not once but twice. Only a drunkard would be the type of person to not use the nearby machine toilet. There's a perfectly good outhouse with a machine toilet right there, but this drunkard is so drunk that he decides to poop under the tree instead. And not only does he poop once, he poops twice.
reading_mnemonic: Oh, I see — the door to the outhouse with the machine toilet is locked, and the drunkard doesn't have the key (き). If he had a machine like a jackhammer, or a circular saw, or some other heavy duty machine, he might be able to get in without a key, but since he has none of those or a key, he's reduced to pooping under the tree instead.
radical_breakdown: 木|Tree, 幺|Poop, 戈|Drunkard, 人|Person

meaning_mnemonic: The fly radical and the fly kanji are exactly the same! Awesome!
reading_mnemonic: When you fly, you generate a lot of heat (ひ) because you’re moving so fast through the atmosphere. Normally this heat would be a nuisance, but you’re a superhero so it doesn’t bother you. This is actually the reason you’re able to fly – you’re a superhero and super resistant to heat.

meaning_mnemonic: You slip off the roof, your life flashes before your eyes, and you smash your mouth on the ground causing some serious damage. Oof, this is a really bad injury, you fell all the way off the roof and onto your mouth.
reading_mnemonic: As you try to assess the damage, you hear someone shout, "Guy (がい), hey, you okay, guy?" They run up to you, but your mouth is too damaged, you can't respond. "Okay guy, I'm gonna call you Guy now. Let's get you to the hospital."

meaning_mnemonic: Regardless of whether or not you wear a hat while you jackhammer, you’re going to have a surplus of noise. Jackhammers are loud, and your hat is doing nothing to dampen the racket. There’s a surplus of commotion coming from the jackhammer and onlookers are not amused.
reading_mnemonic: One of the people walking by is the owner of a push cart yo-yo (よ) stand. Having a surplus of yo-yos, he starts throwing them at you. This makes you stop using the jackhammer as you need both hands to fend off the yo-yo barrage.

meaning_mnemonic: A Chinese turkey is difficult to find because they are so rare. Chinese turkeys are the rarest variety of turkey, so naturally, finding one is exceedingly difficult.
reading_mnemonic: Do you know the actual reason Chinese turkey are so difficult to find? It’s because they’re all made out of Naan (なん). Of course they’re elusive when they blend in so well with all the other Naan!

meaning_mnemonic: That outfit on your skin is there to cover you up. In polite society, it's expected that you cover your skin with some kind of outfit — even if you have to wear something that causes you to incur damage, like circulation-cutting skinny jeans or a shirt with a really scratchy tag.
reading_mnemonic: Another reason to cover yourself is to retain heat (ひ). Actually, retaining heat and staying warm is probably the reason people started covering themselves up in the first place.

meaning_mnemonic: You take a stone to the forehead of a turkey. It is certain that you will damage it.
reading_mnemonic: You're killing this turkey, and you need to make sure he's dead for certain. The reason you need to make sure this turkey is dead is because of the cock (かく) in your life. Male chickens get really jealous when turkeys are around.

meaning_mnemonic: The leader's mouth has grown old from saying so many things. This is what makes them different from everyone else, they speak truly like an individual.
reading_mnemonic: As an individual, they must teach all the 子s (こ) their way. Their individual way.

meaning_mnemonic: A narwhal sticks a stick into the dirt to see what might exist underneath it. Narwhals live in the sea, you see. So they're convinced nothing can exist anywhere else.
reading_mnemonic: The narwhal can't find anything but it can't stop thinking about what could exist outside of its world. It pulls out a xylophone (ざい) and starts tapping the keys with its horn. It plays a sad song about the meaning of life and whether existence is worth it.

meaning_mnemonic: A flowers net is upon your forehead in the evening. These appear on your head at night whenever you are having a dream.
reading_mnemonic: You dream about cows saying "moo (む), moo, moo!"
radical_breakdown: 艹|Flowers, 罒|Net, 冖|Forehead, 夕|Evening

meaning_mnemonic: You stand on the Cliff of Life and give birth to a child. Oh no! You’re standing too close to the edge of the Cliff of Life! The baby falls off the cliff right after you give birth to it! In your despair, you throw all your property off the cliff too.
reading_mnemonic: You give birth, and now this happens. Such bad luck. But wait! What's that sound? Sleigh bells? Could it be?! It's Santa-san (さん)! He caught your baby! And all your property.

meaning_mnemonic: Someone stabbed the leader mole with a knife to overthrow it. Now there is a new mole leader. Because that's what happens when you overthrow someone—someone else needs to take over. In this case, a vengeful mole.
reading_mnemonic: Where do leaders get overthrown the most? In とうきょう. Just think back in Japanese history, back when everyone was at war with one another. People were taking over and getting overthrown and then that guy gets overthrown and then THAT guy gets overthrown. Basically, it used to be hard to stay a leader in とうきょう.

meaning_mnemonic: You place a cross on a Wolverine woman. She's gone now, but she was once your wife.
reading_mnemonic: Wait a minute… She can't be dead because your wife is a cyborg (さい)! How could you forget?!

meaning_mnemonic: What you say is righteousness, at least that's what you believe. You keep talking and saying these things, and you don't listen to anyone else's words. This is your style of deliberation and discussion.
reading_mnemonic: What are you in deliberation about? Whether or not to send some poor soul to the guillotine (ぎ). "I think he should go," you say. "I don't think he should," says another. This deliberation is going nowhere...

meaning_mnemonic: In the animal kingdom, a snake is the most likely to commit a crime. Remember the Garden of Eden? The snake was the bad guy. Ever since then, snakes are the animal most known for committing crimes.
reading_mnemonic: This snake has evaded the law for too long. It’s time for a true hero to put an end to its crime spree. Enter Han (はん) Solo. Han Solo is the only man strong and brave enough to put an end to this snake and his crime filled ways.

meaning_mnemonic: Put a net around a criminal to show their guilt. Criminals look like anyone else on the street, so you decide to tie them in nets to make sure people know who they're dealing with.
reading_mnemonic: The guilt shows on the criminal's face. They smile, shrug, and pull a stolen xylophone (ざい) out of their back pocket.

meaning_mnemonic: If there is a building in the direction you want to go it will prevent you from going any further. Like, come on kid, you think you can just walk right through a building? Don't make me laugh!
reading_mnemonic: The building is preventing you from going the right direction, so you pull a bowling (ぼう) ball out of your bag, aim, and bowl the building over. The building, and all the ones around it, go tumbling down. But now the rubble is preventing you from going further.

meaning_mnemonic: You say, throwing your hat on the ground in front of the bookshelf, "I have a theory!" All this reading and thinking has finally given you a wonderful idea, a theory you think might solve all of your problems!
reading_mnemonic: "What is your theory, Ron (ろん)?" asks Hermione. You're Ron Weasley, and you just came up with a theory that you think will help you stop Voldemort.

meaning_mnemonic: Tying a thread to a tombstone each year will help you manage the passage of time. That way you’ll know how many years you pass through, since you’ll have one thread for each year to count.
reading_mnemonic: Dealing with the passage of time can be tough, so after you tie the thread to the tombstone, each year you eat a piece of cake (けい). You already eat cake to mark the passage of time on your birthday, so why not here as well?

meaning_mnemonic: You see a tsunami that's simultaneous (with another tsunami, I assume) and you know the world is about to come to an end.
reading_mnemonic: Just as the world is about to come to an end, your cyborg (さい) appears and blocks it with its cyborg body!

meaning_mnemonic: A grain woman is a woman who talks about grain with other women on a committee. Together they're known as the Committee of Grain Women. What does this committee discuss, you wonder.
reading_mnemonic: Well, they formed this committee because eagles (い) have been eating all the grain. The women meet as a committee and try to come up with ways to stop these pesky eagles from eating all the grain and leaving none for the humans.

meaning_mnemonic: I hereby cut your assets in half with a knife, says the judge. At someone's divorce proceedings. Ah, the oldest judge trick in the book.
reading_mnemonic: This judge is Han (はん) Solo, so you know he's not going to back down.

meaning_mnemonic: Cows, using nothing more than a towel and a knife, have taken control of the world. Their system of control is brutal — payback for how we humans have treated them, I guess.
reading_mnemonic: It's time to take control back from the cows! Pull out your saber (せい) and fight back!

meaning_mnemonic: You use a special spear in winter to give yourself the power to do all of your tasks.
reading_mnemonic: Your task is to spear this cow. "Moo (む)!" it yells at you and runs away. You need to make dinner though... that's your task, so you better catch up to that cow and put an end to its mooing.

meaning_mnemonic: If a tree is growing out of a top hat you need to inspect it to find out why and how this happened. You should probably investigate the area too. I mean, how could a tree grow out of a top hat anyway? Seems suspicious.
reading_mnemonic: As you inspect the tree, you pick up a saw(さ) and start cutting it. You need to investigate how the tree and the top hat are connected, and a saw is the only way to do it properly.

meaning_mnemonic: Taking out your thread, you sew together the public's hearts to make them whole again.
reading_mnemonic: Once their hearts are whole, the public's soul (そう) becomes one!

meaning_mnemonic: If you say a new weapon idea out loud, then it will be established immediately.
reading_mnemonic: Weapons have to be established in sets (せつ). So you have to make another one that goes with it. Make them cohesive please.

meaning_mnemonic: The next shellfish will be yours, but this shellfish will be mine. These are the resources we have to share and distribute.
reading_mnemonic: You save up all of your resources so you can buy a sheep (し). You bring a big sack of your shellfish resources to the market and finally get to pick out that sheep you've had your eyes on for months.

meaning_mnemonic: Under a tree, a broken arrow protrudes from a turkey. It was fighting for the rights of its fellow turkeys, and was mortally wounded in the process.
reading_mnemonic: "You have rights, so I won't shoot you like this turkey," says the voice of Ken (けん) the samurai, from above you in the tree.

meaning_mnemonic: The leader of the cow tribe is too important to deal with small matters and trivial affairs.
reading_mnemonic: All of his affairs are taken care of by Ken (けん) the samurai, who he hired as his underling.

meaning_mnemonic: A lion harvesting rice uses an axe to cut off the tops of the stalks. The lion is roaming the rice fields using his axe to harvest the rice. He does so by cutting off the part of the rice stalks he needs.
reading_mnemonic: The lion will cut off rice stalks until dawn (だん). But at the first light of dawn, it will run and hide in the shade of the trees, cut off from the rice.

meaning_mnemonic: Both a leader and a king have a duty to protect their people. A good leader always protects his followers, and a good king always protects his subjects. This is their duty.
reading_mnemonic: You’re the village nincompoop (にん), but the king and the leader still have a duty to protect you. Even a nincompoop is important to the kings and leaders of the world.

meaning_mnemonic: The life of a shellfish is filled with blame. They take the blame for everything from food poisoning and allergies, to cutting people's feet on beaches.
reading_mnemonic: When those poor shellfish aren't having blame piled on them, they're being eaten, because shellfish are thought to make for a very sexy (せき) meal.

meaning_mnemonic: The dirt mask is a mask which, when put on, will greatly increase the amount of dirt.
reading_mnemonic: Use the dirt mask to increase the dirt around you. The zombies (ぞう) are trying to escape, so you just keep increasing the dirt on top of them so they can't get out.

meaning_mnemonic: Some of your grain has just been taken by a guard. This is the tax you pay for living in this town. Back in the day, grain was used like currency, so it makes sense that guards went around collecting grain tax.
reading_mnemonic: You have to pay this tax, because if you don't the guard will cut you down with his special German saber, a zeiber (ぜい). "Don't you hear vat I zei? Pay ze tax or I vill zlei you vis my zeiber!" he shouts.

meaning_mnemonic: Angle your sword correctly at this cow to solve its riddle. The key is to untie the cow with the sword without hurting it.
reading_mnemonic: Did I mention that you have to solve this whole riddle while on a kayak (かい)? No?! Whoops.

meaning_mnemonic: Buildings hold festivals on special occasions.
reading_mnemonic: The occasion this time is to celebrate your wonderful cyborg (さい). It's about time you did something nice for it.

meaning_mnemonic: Whatever people say to you will be carved by a blade into your heart. Sounds cruel, but it's a way to make you recognize their power.
reading_mnemonic: Having their words carved into your heart makes you recognize the authority of many people. But the only one you could ever truly acknowledge, is Nintendo (にん).

meaning_mnemonic: While riding on your scooter, you grow a mustache on top of the mustache you already have in order to surpass the people around you. You're in a scooter race and your mustache is the only thing keeping you in the lead, but someone else has a mustache too! So you grow another mustache to surpass them once again!
reading_mnemonic: Suddenly, something else manages to surpass you all. It's a car (か)! A car with two mustaches is also riding on a scooter and going way faster than you.

meaning_mnemonic: From the roof, an icicle falls and hits Wolverine in the forehead, and he has to go over to the stool to lie down. And eventually he goes to sleep.
reading_mnemonic: While wolverine sleeps, he makes a horrible neighing (ね) sound. It's like there's a giant horse in his mouth screaming to get out! NEIGH NEIGH!
radical_breakdown: 宀|Roof, 丬|Icicle, ヨ|Wolverine, 冖|Forehead, 又|Stool

meaning_mnemonic: You kiss each and every one of your best pals to show them how much you love and care for them. You kiss each friend right on the mouth.
reading_mnemonic: Actually, each and every one of your best pals is of the cock (かく) variety. By that, I mean each of them is a rooster. Imagine kissing each cock on its beak.

meaning_mnemonic: You need your net to be straight before you put it on the ground and try to lure something into it. You put your net there to catch something, but if it's twisted or tangled, it won't be very effective.
reading_mnemonic: Then you decide to put cheese (ち) in your net. With a perfectly straight net and the cheese you put down as bait, there’s no way this fails. Success is all about how you put the net down and the cheese you put in it.

meaning_mnemonic: Dollars and shellfish are used to pay expenses and costs. Shellfish used to be used as currency, so they're like the coins that go with dollars.
reading_mnemonic: What is the biggest expense and cost? It's the heat (ひ) bill.

meaning_mnemonic: The womb is a circle of power where a force of nature is formed. The womb has the power to create life. Life is a force of nature, and the circle of life starts in the womb.
reading_mnemonic: Now pretend you're the mother. You'll need all the force you can muster to bring that baby into the world, so you grab hold of your special saber (せい) and slice it about in the air to give you the extra force you need.

meaning_mnemonic: A Viking who knows how to use a bathtub will have to manage all the baths for the other Vikings. Vikings aren't so great with bathing... if you can get one Viking to figure it out he has to manage the rest of them.
reading_mnemonic: The poor Viking trying to manage all the others keeps having to confiscate acorns (えい). "You can't take baths in acorns and wood, it has to be water!" he shouts.

meaning_mnemonic: You can use a jackhammer to indicate and show someone where the prize is buried. You buried the prize to keep it safe, but the jackhammer is great at unearthing it. Jackhammers do a great job and show where the treasure lies. They indicate quite clearly where one needs to go.
reading_mnemonic: Actually, you're unearthing Jesus (じ). He’s the treasure. For your soul. He’s here to show you that Jesus is still a hip and cool guy and he wants to indicate to you that having faith in Jesus and God and stuff is super rad. Jesus is all like, “Who has two thumbs and wants to show you the way of the Lord? This guy.”

meaning_mnemonic: Taking orders from a geoduck will place you into enemy territory. Geoducks make terrible commanders, so if you take orders from one, expect to end up in unknown territory, potentially even enemy territory. Be prepared.
reading_mnemonic: Not wanting to end up dead in enemy territory, you decide to escape this geoduck leader by getting on a row (りょう) boat and rowing your way outta there. The geoduck commander orders you to halt your escape, but you still get in your row boat and row away.

meaning_mnemonic: That scarecrow with the knife is the vice president. Yeah, I know how he looks, and I'm pretty sure he does some murdering on the side, but you didn't hear that from me.
reading_mnemonic: It's the vice president's turn to speak at the podium and he just clears his throat and yells, "F**k (ふく) you!" to the crowd, holding up his knife. They cheer.

meaning_mnemonic: There's an arrow in a turkey that you can see in your view. The turkey seems to be viewing you too, from afar.
reading_mnemonic: As you view the turkey, Genghis Khan (かん) suddenly comes into your view too. He towers over the injured turkey, leans down, and... pulls the arrow out!?

meaning_mnemonic: A great leader can look straight at something and know its value. That social media site? 44 billion dollars. That job position? 50k a year. A four-day work week? Um… sorry, no, there's no value there. See? Leaders can see straight to the heart of matters to grasp something's true value.
reading_mnemonic: One thing your leader knows has great value is cheese (ち). Say goodbye to your days of casually snacking on cheesy treats from the conbini, because your leader's decided the value of cheese is going up 1000%!

meaning_mnemonic: Your mouth is like an escalator you use to suck and inhale things into your body.
reading_mnemonic: Use this mouth ability to suck cucumbers (きゅう) into your mouth. Cucumbers are shaped like cylinders so you can suck them into your mouth like this. Just as nature intended.

meaning_mnemonic: Lying in the dirt, a drunkard puts her mouth to the ground to understand the region. She loves to know all the regional differences among wines and other alcohols, and to her there's no better way to do this than putting her mouth on the ground and literally tasting each region.
reading_mnemonic: Turns out she thinks everything from this region is icky (いき). In fact, to the drunkard, every region tastes icky and gross. You don't have the heart to tell her it's the dirt and ground, not the region itself, that tastes icky…
radical_breakdown: 土|Dirt, 戈|Drunkard, 口|Mouth, 一|Ground

meaning_mnemonic: See all those icicles to the dog's left? Good thing they all fell on his left, or he would've been in a terrible condition.
reading_mnemonic: What saved the dog's condition was none other than Joe (じょう), the local farmhand. He constantly keeps an eye on the dog's condition, including any dangerously sharp icicles that could descend on him.

meaning_mnemonic: Wrap vines around a stool to obtain it. Don't worry about paying for it, sneak into the stool store and tie some vines around the legs. Then when you leave, pull the vines and the stool will come out after. That's how you obtain a stool!
reading_mnemonic: Today you want to obtain a new pair of shoes (しゅう). You tie your vines around the stool they're on, and slowly inch them toward the door.

meaning_mnemonic: The leather radical and the leather kanji are exactly the same! Cool!
reading_mnemonic: One way to get leather is to skin a male chicken, a cock (かく). Not a very efficient way to get leather, but one way nonetheless.

meaning_mnemonic: Reaching your ear is the sound of a drunkard who can’t find employment. You hear him before you see him because he’s behind some trash cans. Being a drunkard, he’s like, super wasted and just kind of rambling to himself, making strange sounds. No wonder he can’t find employment.
reading_mnemonic: Since this guy is such a pathetic drunkard, it comes as no shock (しょく) that he can’t find employment. If he did find employment, I would be filled with both shock and awe.

meaning_mnemonic: A man who is husband material can see a standard woman and think she’s the greatest thing ever. This man will make a great husband. Even though the lady is pretty standard, the husband treats her like she’s anything but.
reading_mnemonic: It’s pretty standard for a husband and wife to exchange vows when getting married, and the husband said this girl held the key (き) to his heart. She unlocked the husband’s heart with the key and now he’s a man made whole.

meaning_mnemonic: Under the roof of life a mouth with a knife divides cells to create life.
reading_mnemonic: As it divides life, the mouth begins to look really familiar. It has big teeth and a crooked mustache... it's Wario (わり)! Sometimes Wario cuts himself by accident and just becomes わ (which is all he says too).
radical_breakdown: 宀|Roof, 生|Life, 口|Mouth, 刂|Knife

meaning_mnemonic: There's going to be a tsunami. So you get up on your roof. You see people across the street, in a rice paddy. They watch as you put on a pair of fins. And you begin acting. This is your last chance to perform!
reading_mnemonic: As the acting ends (えん), so do you all.
radical_breakdown: 氵|Tsunami, 宀|Roof, 丁|Street, 田|Rice Paddy, ハ|Fins
component_names: Tsunami, Roof, Street, Rice Paddy, Fins

meaning_mnemonic: A drop of water falls from a bear onto the ground and needs to be wiped up with a towel. Only a teacher or an expert could get away with getting close to this wet bear to wipe up after it.
reading_mnemonic: The teacher tells you to start with something smaller, after all, you're not an expert yet. You have to practice on a wet sheep (し). "I became a wet, dangerous animal expert by starting with sheep, you will too!" your teacher says.
radical_breakdown: 丶|Drop, 㠯|Bear, 一|Ground, 巾|Towel

meaning_mnemonic: Riding a tsunami you see a turkey carrying a cross, but that’s pretty standard here. This is your dreamland. You always dream about tsunamis and the turkeys carrying crosses that ride them. This might be strange for other people, but for you it’s pretty normal.
reading_mnemonic: These wacky dreams are only standard fare in June (じゅん) though. You don’t have them any other time of the year, just in June. You don’t know why June is the only time you have dreams about tsunami riding turkeys, but that’s just the way it is.

meaning_mnemonic: The leader put flowers on a cliff. That is their task. It is to provide and equip the cliff with flowers.
reading_mnemonic: Why do they provide and equip the cliff with flowers? It's all for the bees (び).

meaning_mnemonic: Take this road's measurement. Hmm. It seems a bit too long. As you measure it, you continue down this road, wondering where it will lead you.
reading_mnemonic: Where does the road that you're measuring lead to? To a doughnut (どう) shop!

meaning_mnemonic: The leader of a hundred foreheads in the heart of winter is superior at being gentle. These hundred foreheads are sensitive, especially in the heart of winter, so the leader must be very gentle. Not just any kind of gentle though—the superior kind of gentle that will keep a hundred foreheads following.
reading_mnemonic: You need to be superior because all of these foreheads belong to youths (ゆう). They don't know how to take care of themselves, though they try to convince you they can. They're too young to know any better.
radical_breakdown: ｲ|Leader, 百|Hundred, 冖|Forehead, 心|Heart, 夂|Winter

meaning_mnemonic: You need to go up on the roof and use it like a slide seven times to make this your house. A house isn't a home until you've slid down its roof exactly seven times, you know.
reading_mnemonic: When you slide down the roof of your house, you end up with a tack (たく) in your butt cheek. All the roof shingles on your new home are attached with tacks, so it's honestly a miracle that you only got one tack stuck in you.

meaning_mnemonic: The king can see the present time for what it really is. The future isn't important. The past isn't important. The present is when everything appears.
reading_mnemonic: At the present time the king is Genji (げん). The time has finally come for him to get serious, and as they say, there's no time like the present.

meaning_mnemonic: A mouth that wants peace can call for it. If you don’t have a mouth, you can’t call for peace. So use your mouth and call for peace when you can. Peace is great.
reading_mnemonic: But before you call for peace, you must first placate the masses. To do so, you astound them with your yo-yo (よ) skills. Once they are so entranced by how talented you are with a yo-yo, you easily convince them to make peace.

meaning_mnemonic: You use your fingers at dawn to carry many things. You have to carry yourself out of bed. You have to carry your backpack or purse or laptop bag to school or work. Your fingers have to carry a lot of weight around at dawn.
reading_mnemonic: Once you're carrying everything, and the dawn sun is shining bright, you start getting tan (たん). Especially those fingers you're using to carry things.

meaning_mnemonic: When you're a guest somewhere it's important to bring geoducks. But more than that, the amount of geoducks you bring is really what matters. If you don't have any live geoducks go ahead and bring any amount of framed pictures of geoducks instead.
reading_mnemonic: Unfortunately, if you mess up the amount or the framed pictures, every other guest will gawk (がく) at you.

meaning_mnemonic: You take your scooter to Korea and everything is different!
reading_mnemonic: What's also different is that there's a weird tiger bouncing on its tail alongside you yelling that its name is Tigger (ちが). You didn't know Tigger was living in Korea these days. That's definitely different.

meaning_mnemonic: What does a car and the Death Star have in common? They're both used to transport people and things.
reading_mnemonic: Right now you and the Death Star are transporting yurts (ゆ). They're the universe's #1 best transportable homes!

meaning_mnemonic: When a sheep tries its hoof at construction, it gains distinction. Now that is something that really sets a sheep apart! After all, have you ever seen a sheep working in construction?
reading_mnemonic: The extra distinction of this sheep is that its really skilled with a saw (さ). That's why it's so good at construction.

meaning_mnemonic: The elephant radical and the elephant kanji are the same. But! This kanji has another meaning: phenomenon. If you were the first person to see an elephant, you'd call it that too.
reading_mnemonic: Elephants are great and all, except that when they die they turn into elephant zombies (ぞう). But you never see these zombies because the shougun (しょう) has a special project in place that destroys all elephant bodies when they die. Hint: The readings and meanings for this kanji match up really nicely. ぞう is always for elephant and しょう is always for phenomenon. Remember it like this, the elephant is the zombie and the shougun keeps everyone from finding out about this phenomenon.

meaning_mnemonic: The dirt where you just stand and see is a boundary. You don't want to cross the boundary, you just stand there and see over it. As a general rule, you can stand in the dirt and see beyond boundaries, but you don't usually cross them.
reading_mnemonic: The boundary you're looking at now is the Kyoto (きょう) boundary. Kyoto is one of the most famous places in Japan, so you can imagine its boundary is really clear and marked by all kinds of boundary signs that say KYOTO.

meaning_mnemonic: On the ground there's a ceremony where everyone keeps stopping. This stopping ceremony is being performed by the military. They'll march one direction, then stop and turn, then march another direction, then stop again.
reading_mnemonic: You look closer at the people in the military and realize that every time they stop they take a drink of booze (ぶ)!

meaning_mnemonic: You have to use two axes to open these shellfish. That seems like overkill, but it is necessary. These particular shellfish are of very high quality meaning they won't open so easily.
reading_mnemonic: You finally get all of the shellfish open and you're admiring their quality, when your shih tzu (しつ) jumps up on the table and gobbles them down. NO! You try to chase after the little dog, but it's too late. They're gone.

meaning_mnemonic: On this scooter, there's an angel with a drop of sweat coming off of it, because it forgot to mention something to you! It seems like it's something important too, since they're sweating so much.
reading_mnemonic: "I forgot to mention, you have to study ninjutsu (じゅつ)!" the angel yells. But it's too late, there are ninjas jumping out of the bushes around you and taking you hostage.

meaning_mnemonic: When a leader wants to work together, it means they want what you have to offer. Congrats! Now you can accompany them everywhere and offer them hot towels and bottled water, or whatever it is you do…
reading_mnemonic: Once a year, the leader will offer you a vacation in きょうと. It's an all-expenses-paid trip! The catch is that you have to accompany your leader to きょうと…

meaning_mnemonic: A building's roots will limit the things under and around it.
reading_mnemonic: The person who hates these limits more than anyone else is Genji (げん). He wants to be able to tunnel under buildings, sneak in, smooch ladies, and sneak back out. But all the building root limits make that impossible!

meaning_mnemonic: A beggar lies sprawled on the ground so you give him some money. You feel bad for the beggar on the ground, so that’s why you decided to give him something.
reading_mnemonic: When you set the money down next to the beggar he shouts, “No! I want a yo-yo (よ)!” so you go to the corner store and buy him a yo-yo with the money instead. You give the yo-yo to the beggar and he looks very happy.

meaning_mnemonic: A tsunami carries your yurt and you on a stool under it away. You are now in transit.
reading_mnemonic: The transit of yourself and your yurt home is due to the water (わた). This is water transit.

meaning_mnemonic: The sun rises over the capital, creating a scene of breathtaking beauty. The sun is bright and warm as it crests over the capital. It’s quite the scene to behold.
reading_mnemonic: The only way to make this scene better would be to add cake (けい). Now that you think about it, as the sun rises and frosts the capital with light, the buildings start to look like big, shiny cakes.

meaning_mnemonic: Touch your fingers to your friend to pull out their friendship. Pull it out with a high five. Pull it out with a back rub. Pull it out with an, "Oh no, there's some lint on your shirt, let me get that for you."
reading_mnemonic: Your friend looks you in the eye and says, I want you to pull out my hair. I want my head to be nude (ぬ). Now you have to use your fingers on your friend to pull out their hair and make their head all nude.

meaning_mnemonic: The outfit you wear at your wedding is a supplement to the occasion. It's not as important as the vows or the kiss or anything, but a sharp tux and a gorgeous dress really supplement the festive mood and get everyone into "wedding mode."
reading_mnemonic: You decide to further supplement your wedding outfit with a garden hoe (ほ). This hoe is a symbolic supplement — it represents the new life you'll "cultivate" together with your partner.

meaning_mnemonic: A leader with a stick, a hook, and an arrow is able to change the climate and weather. Not just the type of climate that causes sunny and rainy days though, the political climate too, because they're a political candidate too.
reading_mnemonic: Who is this climate and weather-changing candidate leader with the hook, stick, and arrow? It's none other than こういち.

meaning_mnemonic: A tree is what a lifeguard uses to set up the station where he'll care for the people on the beach and in the water. Trees provide the shade lifeguards need to take care of half-drowned kids and grannies with sand stuck in their bathing suits. That's why they set up their care stations here.
reading_mnemonic: You look closer at the set up and realize the lifeguard is こういち! You know he teaches Japanese but... is こういち really qualified to care for people like this?

meaning_mnemonic: Use your fingers at your wedding to catch anything thrown at you. Catch the bouquet, for example, or catch the rice everyone throws at you. Weddings are really more about catching things with your fingers than they are about whoever is standing across from you.
reading_mnemonic: You're having a good time catching things until it's cleanup time and someone throws a hoe (ほ) at you. First of all, ouch, that was your face. Second, this is your wedding. You aren't supposed to have to hoe it all up. You're supposed to drop everything you caught and leave!

meaning_mnemonic: If you could just get your soul to open the window to shellfish, you'll grow accustomed to them sooner or later! I know shellfish are a bit of an acquired taste, but if you don't open that window, you'll never like them!
reading_mnemonic: You'll need to become accustomed to eating shellfish if you want to grow up big and strong like Genghis Khan (かん). He didn't have shellfish growing up either you know, he had to grow accustomed to their taste too, but look how successful he was!

meaning_mnemonic: If a tsunami hits these flowers they'll both become full of water. Tsunamis carry a lot of water, definitely enough to make both of these flowers full.
reading_mnemonic: As you stare at the full flowers, you decide to write a manga (まん) about them. Your head is full of manga ideas!

meaning_mnemonic: Someone covered your fingers with dirt and also got dirt on your toes. So you're going to hang them upside-down and slap them with your dirty extremities.
reading_mnemonic: You hang this person upside-down but they don't seem to be suffering enough, so you hit them with your car (か). No mercy.

meaning_mnemonic: The flag is old but that doesn't mean it's not still alive. This is a living flag, and it gets old just like other living things.
reading_mnemonic: The flag that is old and alive is actually a Buddhist relic (that's why it's alive, in fact ... and old!). But, it's a really dumb relic, so it's put in Little Kyoto (きょ).

meaning_mnemonic: "A scooter!" you announce. You are announcing this because you decided this is what you would create.
reading_mnemonic: But, a scooter has been created before. What is different about yours? The scooter you will create is specifically designed to keep zombies (ぞう) busy.

meaning_mnemonic: You loiter around a black hole, waiting for it to finish destroying and switch to restore mode. You were told all black holes finish eventually, and when they do you can press a button to restore everything back to the way it was.
reading_mnemonic: Finally there's nothing else for the black hole to eat so you hit the restore button.... but nothing happens. "Oh f**k (ふく) you!" you scream as you realize you were lied to.

meaning_mnemonic: How do you make a hole nice and big? You gotta stab something in it. Just thrust it right in there. And make sure your movements are really sudden. Stabs and thrusts are more effective when they're sudden.
reading_mnemonic: Give that hole one last big stab, now you've totes (とつ) showed that hole who's boss. What did I tell you about the sudden thrust technique? It's totes super effective. Like, totes.

meaning_mnemonic: Under the ground, a head covered in dirt emerges... again! It's not the first time you've seen this buried head, nor is it the last. This dirt-covered head hides beneath the ground wherever you go, and keeps popping up to scare you again and again.
reading_mnemonic: The dirt-covered head asks for help again and again, but you've only got a saw (さ). So you start digging with it, scraping the dirt away, until you see this head has the body of a cyborg (さい)!

meaning_mnemonic: Someone is reaching out with their fingers to call for you. They beckon you closer, this way.
reading_mnemonic: The person beckoning you is the Shougun (しょう). You can't help but obey the Shougun's beckoning call.

meaning_mnemonic: Cut this comb up with your weapon and turn it into the steps for some stairs.
reading_mnemonic: You slowly work to create these stairs, you have to slice up a lot of combs, and at dawn (だん) they are done!

meaning_mnemonic: Inside this moon is a black hole... haha just kidding, it's your belly! It's beautiful and round like the moon and it eats up everything you give it like a black hole. What a good stomach you have!
reading_mnemonic: If you don't treat your belly with respect, when you look down at it, it'll yell, "F**k (ふく) you!" Be nice to your stomach!

meaning_mnemonic: When your sick mama tries to do a task she's filled with pain!
reading_mnemonic: Your mama's pain is too (つう) much for her to handle, so now you have to do all of her tasks too.

meaning_mnemonic: If you're on your scooter and you run over a root, you'll need to retreat. The roots have obviously rejected you, they want you to leave, so you should.
reading_mnemonic: You're trying to retreat by scooting backwards, but the roots grab onto your tie (たい). You try to pull your tie off but it's just getting tighter and tighter around your neck.

meaning_mnemonic: You substitute some shellfish for collateral so your friend will lend you some money. Normally he would ask for something more valuable, but you’ve convinced him to substitute these shellfish for what he would normally take as collateral when lending to people.
reading_mnemonic: You want your friend to lend you some money so you can buy yourself a car (か). You need money and a car a lot more than you need this pile of shellfish, so you’re happy to put them up as collateral for the loan.

meaning_mnemonic: If you're riding your scooter through some rice, it's likely you've gone astray. Also you might be lost.
reading_mnemonic: You got so lost and went so astray you ended up on the Mayflower  (めい), a ship that eventually took you across the Atlantic Ocean. Now you've really, really gone astray.

meaning_mnemonic: Someone just asked you to say which direction they should visit.
reading_mnemonic: You end up saying, "You should visit my home (ほう)." How kind of you!

meaning_mnemonic: A woman sitting on a stool with a broken heart is very angry. She had her heart broken by some jerk and now she’s sitting on the stool, just stewing over the guy and how angry she is with him.
reading_mnemonic: As you're sitting on that stool feeling angry, your dog (ど) comes up to console you. He nuzzles his head into your lap, and you start to feel the anger melt away.

meaning_mnemonic: Closing each eye is something that the peoples do before they sleep. The peoples can’t sleep with both eyes open and they can’t sleep with just one eye open either. Peoples have to close each eye before they can sleep.
reading_mnemonic: The reason you want to sleep is because all the other peoples were mean (みん) to you. They were so mean that the only way you could get over it was to close your eyes and sleep. You just want to sleep.

meaning_mnemonic: Take your leather and change it into shoes.
reading_mnemonic: Some shoes aren’t made from leather anymore these days, but you know who always wears shoes made of leather? Old coots (くつ). Old coots are so old that the only shoes they wore growing up were made from leather so they refuse to wear any shoes that aren’t made from leather. Crazy old coots.

meaning_mnemonic: When you ride a scooter you'll have a surplus of possible routes. Not only can you drive on any road, but you can ride on the sidewalk too!
reading_mnemonic: You decide to take the fastest route, since you have so many options, and drive on the sidewalk. However, in doing so you run over every single toe (と) on every single person trying to walk there.

meaning_mnemonic: Your threads have to suit you if you want a good salary. No one is going to give you a salary if your clothes don't suit you. You have to look professional!
reading_mnemonic: Your salary is paid in cucumbers (きゅう). Maybe you shouldn't have worn that cucumber tie when you interviewed for this job, even though it suited you well.

meaning_mnemonic: You got your ice orders. Of course, your ice orders are to make things cool and cold.
reading_mnemonic: How will you make things cool and cold? You'll use a special ray (れい) gun that shoots a cold ray.

meaning_mnemonic: A winter table would be an odd thing to deal with. Winter can be hard to deal with on its own, but turn your table into winter? Just dealing with your food getting cold would be the worst!
reading_mnemonic: This winter table is something you have to deal with, sure, but what if you just gave it to a circus show (しょ)? They like weird stuff like this.

meaning_mnemonic: See that woman with the broom? That's the lady of the house. She's getting ready to hand that broom to you — her butler — because you missed a spot over there.
reading_mnemonic: Instead of your name, the lady of the house just calls you "fool" (ふ). You rarely meet her ladyship's lofty standards, so from her perspective you're just a silly nincompoop fool who can't get anything right.

meaning_mnemonic: A grain, from one evening to the next evening, experiences a shift. After two evenings, the grain has shifted from one location to another.
reading_mnemonic: This shift is caused by the eagle (い) that wants to eat the grains. Every other evening, the eagle swoops down, shifts the grains (eating a few) and then flies off.

meaning_mnemonic: The Grain Mouth King pours grain from his mouth for you and his other subjects. You go to him and pull his finger. When you do this, grain pours from his mouth. But we were greedy. We didn't understand the extent to which we were harvesting his mouth wheat.
reading_mnemonic: The extent to which we were harvesting grain from his mouth was too great. The Grain Mouth King has run out of grain. He worries he will lose power if he has no grain to offer, so he switches to barfing out tater (てい) tots instead.

meaning_mnemonic: Rice that is blue has a strong spirit. Our spirits are blue, so if you ever see rice (or other food, or even people) that's blue, you know that's their spirit radiating out!
reading_mnemonic: You want to see the spirit up close, so you take your saber (せい), throw the blue rice in the air, and slice it in half! The rice explodes and blue light fills everything! Then it's gone.

meaning_mnemonic: Sometime in the future, thread of every color will be faced with extinction. Eventually there will be nothing else to make thread out of, and thread of every kind and color will reach extinction.
reading_mnemonic: The extinction of thread was brought on by a very strange thing. Deadly zits (ぜつ). These zits killed off all the producers of thread, and eventually the thread went extinct. Dang zits.

meaning_mnemonic: A tree is not a cup of liquid or a counter for cups. Don’t get them mixed up. The last time you tried making a cup out of a tree to count your throat got filled with splinters when you used it. There wasn't even any liquid in it.
reading_mnemonic: Another way to remember the counter for cups using a cup of liquid would be by creating and memorizing a haiku (はい) about them. Aren’t haikus useful?

meaning_mnemonic: A district that lacks things will be in Europe.
reading_mnemonic: Europe is lacking so much because their 王 (おう) keeps taking everything.

meaning_mnemonic: Grains get blamed for how much they accumulate. If the grains accumulate too much then they make more work for the farmers. If they accumulate too little, then they're starving the people. Ugh, grains just can't win with you people. They're blamed for everything.
reading_mnemonic: Now the grains have accumulated a ton, they're overflowing in their grain sacks, and the farmer freezes and says, "Now those are some sexy (せき) grains."

meaning_mnemonic: Under this roof someone odd is trying to draw near to you. You back up, but they continue to draw near anyway.
reading_mnemonic: They continue to draw near until you can't take it anymore. You run out from under the roof, slam the door closed, and lock it with a key (き).

meaning_mnemonic: A woman who is good is my daughter. My daughter is a good woman, I guarantee it.
reading_mnemonic: Your daughter, on the other hand, is not a good woman. Your daughter looks like a moose who may (むすめ) not be able to find its way out of a wet paper bag. Your daughter looks like a moose who may lose its way without a map. Your daughter looks like a moose who may do lots of stupid things.

meaning_mnemonic: The soul of a narwhal was sucked into its towel, which is scary!
reading_mnemonic: As you watch this scary scene you can't help but mutter, "Fool," (ふ) under your breath. Then you hear "Fool, fool, fool, it's too scary you fool!" and you realize all of the other narwhals are chanting.

meaning_mnemonic: A saw cuts into your heart and you are filled with fear. Well, you were filled with fear before the saw reached your heart too, but now that the saw is cutting into your heart, you’re feeling more fear than ever.
reading_mnemonic: Even more so than your fear of dying, you are filled with the fear that you’ll never get to vacation in きょうと. You always wanted to take a trip to きょうと, but if you die from this saw wound to the heart, you’ll never get the chance to go.

meaning_mnemonic: You meet a woman from another clan under the rising sun to prepare for marriage. Your clan and her clan are standing together as the two of you watch the sun rise together.
reading_mnemonic: For the marriage to be official, you need to wait for a condor (こん) to appear. If it doesn't show up before the sun goes down again, the marriage was a failure. You have to try again tomorrow with a different woman.

meaning_mnemonic: On a scooter running in one direction is a gun-toting child. This is a terribly dangerous situation, but to the child it is just play.
reading_mnemonic: Everything is play for youths (ゆう), even if it's a terrible, scary, not good situation like this one.

meaning_mnemonic: Those that can only eat a part of a shellfish are probably a bit poor.
reading_mnemonic: And since they are poor, they are getting these shellfish parts from the trash bin (びん). It's quite unfortunate.

meaning_mnemonic: A scooter with a mohawk, now that's the most suitable hairstyle you could ever think of for a scooter!
reading_mnemonic: You want this suitable hairstyle for your scooter too, and luckily you're a techie (てき), so it's easy for you to install one.

meaning_mnemonic: Take your fingers, put them on this turtle shell, and push push push! Push the turtle right on out of there.
reading_mnemonic: You're trying to push this turtle out so you can use the shell for your new obi (お). You keep seeing other people wearing turtle shell patterns on their obi, but you're going to go a step further. You're going to MAKE your obi out of actual turtle shells! You just have to push this darn turtle out first.

meaning_mnemonic: In the ground of the rice paddy is a treasure. As you pull it out of the mucky ground, you can feel your life force beingrenewed.
reading_mnemonic: Just as you were getting accustomed to this life renewing treasure, こういち comes out of nowhere, stealing your treasure and running off with it.

meaning_mnemonic: A tsunami knocks a cleat off a child and the shoe begins to float away in the water. This child was just out playing soccer, minding his own business, when the tsunami crashed in and knocked his cleats off his feet. Now the cleat is floating away with the tsunami.
reading_mnemonic: While you float in the water, an uni (う) jabs into your foot. “Uwaaa~ (うわ)” you cry. That uni really hurts. They’re all spikey and painful and junk. “Uwaaaa~”

meaning_mnemonic: You run every day and soon you become a human that can go beyond the normal speed limits of man. You run and you run and you run. This training allows you to become super human. You go beyond the limits of a normal human. You become a human who can run really fast.
reading_mnemonic: To solidify your ability to go beyond the abilities of other humans, you etch (えつ) sacred runes into your legs to preserve your running abilities. Etching these runes makes sure that your skills will never deteriorate.

meaning_mnemonic: You fly north to the moon and break your back when you finally land on it. You weren’t braced for impact so when you hit the moon, your back took all of the impact.
reading_mnemonic: Your back hurts so much that the only way to properly explain the pain is in haiku (はい) form. I flew to the moon. It is there I broke my back. My back hurts real bad.

meaning_mnemonic: The next plate is the one you will steal. This one would be too obvious, better wait for the next one.
reading_mnemonic: You steal this plate from a とうきょう restaurant, so after you steal it, picture yourself running through the streets of とうきょう as you lose your pursuers.

meaning_mnemonic: The buildings are at a surplus. Because of that, we will need to exclude some of them from our future plans. Also, we'll need to remove some buildings too.
reading_mnemonic: Working with you on this project to exclude buildings from the plan, as well as remove buildings that already exist is little Jo-Anne (じょ).

meaning_mnemonic: You poop twice on a sleeping drunkard person and you find yourself wondering how many more times you can poop on them and wonder how much they can take before they realize what’s going on.
reading_mnemonic: As you continue thinking about how much poop this drunkard can take and how many more poops you can drop on him, he begins to wake up. Quickly, you eke (いく) out one last poop before you scurry away. You eke that poop out just in time to make your escape.
