meaning_mnemonic: If you play blackjack on the moon in the winter, your cards will scatter everywhere. The cards scatter because the gravity is so weak on the moon, so the blackjack game is prone to disaster.
reading_mnemonic: You are playing blackjack with Santa-san (さん). Santa-san is doing his best to use his Christmas magic to prevent the scatter of cards, but it’s not working out so well. Good effort, Santa-san.

meaning_mnemonic: A leader of (odd-looking) lions puts a drop of magic liquid on his face to look like a person who resembles someone else. The leader of lions is going incognito, so he needs to resemble a person who is not himself. He takes this drop of powerful face paint and transforms.
reading_mnemonic: Now he resembles an even greater leader, and all the lions get down on one knee (に) to pay their respects. (Note that we recently changed this kanji's main reading from ね to に, because ね is an irregular reading.)

meaning_mnemonic: On your roof is a scarecrow because you're rich. You want to scare away all the poor, non-rich people so you put a scarecrow on your roof.
reading_mnemonic: You wake up the next morning and all of your riches have been stolen! You call the police and they call you a fool (ふ)! Pardon me?! "You basically put an advertisement on your roof telling everyone you're rich. Of course you got robbed, you fool."

meaning_mnemonic: Put your fingers to your forehead and stand your legs high up in a tree if you want to look for something. After all, shielding your eyes and getting up high is the best way to look for something, isn’t it?
reading_mnemonic: You look for it for so long that you can't help getting a tan (たん). I mean, you're up some tree, shielding your eyes from the sun as you look for that thing, and it's been hours, days? Of course you're going to get a tan.
radical_breakdown: 扌|Fingers, 冖|Forehead, 儿|Legs, 木|Tree

meaning_mnemonic: In its scooter, a cat pirate scoots up to welcome you!
reading_mnemonic: The cat pirate then launches into a speech about how they welcome all kinds of people. Especially gay (げい) people. He puts a certain emphasis on gay, so you figure that the cat pirate either thinks you're gay or wants you to be.

meaning_mnemonic: You come across a spirit wearing a top hat and it claims to be your ancestor. Well of course, if you remember correctly, all of your ancestors wore top hats when they were alive. This spirit must be your long lost, great great... uh... somebody.
reading_mnemonic: You ask your ancestor what it wants and it points to the soap (そ) by the sink. Soap? It nods at you. I guess your ancestor is here to see the wonders of soap.

meaning_mnemonic: You count nine of them in the tree, each turkey holding something random or miscellaneous. There are nine turkeys in the tree and they’re all holding random, miscellaneous things. How odd.
reading_mnemonic: As if things couldn’t get any more random, Zazu (ざつ) from the Lion King flies into the tree and starts asking the nine turkeys miscellaneous trivia. Zazu always did have a thirst for knowledge, but this is kind of strange.

meaning_mnemonic: A husband and his husband find a shellfish and agree to share it.
reading_mnemonic: Since the husbands were able to agree, Santa-san (さん) believes they’re both good husbands and belong on the good list. Therefore, Santa-san gives them each lots and lots of shellfish for Christmas.

meaning_mnemonic: A Viking and his older brother join a party. They can raid and pillage better in a group like this, so it makes sense that the Viking and his older brother would join a group with other Vikings.
reading_mnemonic: This party has decided to raid とうきょう. It’s a large undertaking, but they have a large group of Vikings on the job. とうきょう doesn’t stand a chance.

meaning_mnemonic: If you get on your scooter and enter somewhere, you’re going into that place.
reading_mnemonic: Once you’ve gone into this place, what do you see? Your 子 (こ)!

meaning_mnemonic: In the valley you feel a lack of want. You want for nothing in this valley. It is the valley of plenty.
reading_mnemonic: Once you get to the valley, you want some protein. Egg yolk (よく) falls from the sky! It’s a miracle! You wanted protein, and egg yolk was presented. It falls right into your open mouth.

meaning_mnemonic: The gate to talent is now closed. In fact, the gate to talent is always closed. It's not like anyone can just waltz in and get themselves some talent. You have to work for it! You have to work hard to get through that closed gate to talent!
reading_mnemonic: Outside the talent gate that's always closed, hay (へい) is piled up to make beds for the people who are still trying to get in. Who knows how long they'll be there outside the closed gate, sleeping in the hay, but they're all working hard to become talented.

meaning_mnemonic: The hole leading to the private heart of your house is the window. Or maybe it's just the window to your soul, and not your house. Like the poetry people say.
reading_mnemonic: You realize that a ton of people are looking into your window and seeing all your private things. This makes you mad (まど)! What right do they have to know your private thoughts and desires?!

meaning_mnemonic: The Not Mouth says “no”. What else would you expect from something named the “Not Mouth”? The Not Mouth will always say “no”, regardless of the question.
reading_mnemonic: You ask the Not Mouth if it is afraid of heat (ひ). The Not Mouth says, “no”. So you set the Not Mouth on fire. The Not Mouth then screams, “NONONONONONONONONONOOOOOO~!” Looks like someone can’t handle the heat.

meaning_mnemonic: A greenhouse is already really good when it comes to a plant's livelihood. But add the sun into that equation and you have something really great for the plants. Their livelihood will be awesome, now!
reading_mnemonic: From out of nowhere, Bobo (ぼ) the notorious clown thief starts picking the plants, ending their livelihood. Bobo needs the flowers for his clown acts, so he uses the livelihood of the flowers to support his own livelihood.

meaning_mnemonic: They say accidentally firing a catapult is an unforgivable mistake. They say you shot the catapult at your own castle. Even though it was an accident, it’s still a mistake you will never be forgiven for.
reading_mnemonic: This mistake alerts Godzilla (ご), who thinks it's town destroying time. He barrels over the hills, sees where you mistakenly catapulted your own people, and proceeds to stomp on the rest of it for you.

meaning_mnemonic: Inside the building is the Winter Cow. You need to see it, so you go inside. It is deep down in there, and you'll have to descend to reach it.
reading_mnemonic: You descend to the bottom and there it is, the Winter Cow. You walk up to the cow, and it swings its head back to see you. Instead of a cow's face, it's こういち's face.

meaning_mnemonic: Boots give you the power to work! That's why so many professions require you to have work boots.
reading_mnemonic: You need boots to give you the power to work for the King (きん) of England. Really, all work is for the King, since everything is for him. But even he wears boots. And they give him the power to uh... king over things.

meaning_mnemonic: A slice with a knife is called a carve.
reading_mnemonic: You work up a sweat trying to carve meat and wood all day, so you grab yourself a nice Coke (こく). You like Coke, and it goes well with meat and sawdust.

meaning_mnemonic: Next to the scooter, there's a flag warning you that there are sheep around here, so you should go slow. That means you might be late, but at least the sheep will be okay!
reading_mnemonic: You follow the flag, but the sheep refuse to slow down so you have to get creative. You place cheese (ち) every ten feet or so, that way the sheep slow down to bend down on their scooters and take a bite.

meaning_mnemonic: If you scrape a sharp stone against your skin, it will tear. The sharp stone tears your skin. It hurts!
reading_mnemonic: The moment your skin tears you can't help but yelp "Ha (は)!" It sounds like a laugh, but it's more like a pained bark.

meaning_mnemonic: The ground and a shuriken have mutual respect for one another. The shuriken respects the ground because of how solid and stable it is, and the ground respects the shuriken for how pointy it is. They have great mutual respect here.
reading_mnemonic: Since you made the shuriken attack the ground, the mutual respect is out of balance. This summons Godzilla (ご) up from the depths of the ocean once more. He always shows up when something is out of wack, to show humans the error of their ways. He picks up the shuriken and flings it into a city, which explodes, leaving a crater in the ground.

meaning_mnemonic: If you loiter around my skin, he will get angry at you. He's my very protective friend, and you don't wanna make him angry!
reading_mnemonic: He may get grumpy if you loiter around my skin, but a well-made curry (かれ) always brightens his mood. So give him some curry.

meaning_mnemonic: Your ear listens to your heart and feels shame. Your heart is full of shame for how you’ve lived your life and when your ear hears all the things you’ve done, your ear feels shame too.
reading_mnemonic: You must cleanse your spirit of this shame. You decide to complete Haj (はじ). (Haj is the fifth pillar of Islam, and is a pilgrimage to Mecca during the month of Dhu al-Hijja). Upon arrival in Mecca, you think of a funny joke and bust out laughing. “HAHAHAHAHAHA!! (は) HAHAHAHAHA!!!” Oh man, you’re in a temple and that was completely inappropriate. You feel even more shame than before.

meaning_mnemonic: Your fingers are private, no one can see them unless they pay! And you decide if what they pay is enough to get a peek.
reading_mnemonic: If someone tries to look without paying, that's harassment (はら)! Nobody gets to see something of yours without proper payment, but more importantly, your consent!

meaning_mnemonic: The nothing dance is still a dance!
reading_mnemonic: To help you do this dance you need some booze (ぶ). Just enough so it's easier to think of nothing, let all your fears go, and dance.

meaning_mnemonic: A bundle of geoducks is something you can always trust.
reading_mnemonic: While you can trust a bundle of geoducks, never ever trust rye (らい) bread.

meaning_mnemonic: This door is big and you need to return it to its rightful owner. This door is too big and important looking to not belong to someone. You need to find its owner and return it to them.
reading_mnemonic: You are in return mode (もど). When you enter this mode, you concentrate only on returning something. Nothing else matters in this mode. You’re in full on return mode.

meaning_mnemonic: Take your fingers and wrap them around another person. This is called a hug. Just make sure you include all the stuff attached to your fingers, like your hands and arms too, otherwise it's more of a squeeze, and we don't want to do that to people.
reading_mnemonic: Who do you love to hug the most? Your dad (だ)! He gives the best hugs. They're warm and big and tight and comforting. The kind of hug dads are really good at giving.

meaning_mnemonic: The kind of thread you'd wrap around someone would have to be a cord. A regular thread wouldn't be strong enough, so you'd definitely use a cord. This can also mean connection, since cords create connections (by tying things together).
reading_mnemonic: Actually, you're tying this cord around someone as part of a show (しょ). What kind of a show? I really shouldn't say. This cord show isn't free, I'll tell you that much.

meaning_mnemonic: You use your scooter when the omen comes so that you can escape.
reading_mnemonic: You decide to escape this omen by weaving in and out of the busy streets of とうきょう. By now, you know とうきょう like the back of your hand, so you're sure you can escape this way.

meaning_mnemonic: You loiter at noon near a stop sign to get a stamp of approval from someone honorable. This honorable personage drives by at noon every day, and because they have to stop at the stop sign, people loiter here for a chance to get their honorable stamp of approval.
reading_mnemonic: The honorable personage is Godzilla (ご). Actually, you're requesting Godzilla's stamp of approval for a new demolition job in downtown Tokyo. Godzilla is the god of urban demolition, what with all those cities it's destroyed, and you need its honorable approval to continue.
radical_breakdown: 彳|Loiter, 午|Noon, 止|Stop, 卩|Stamp

meaning_mnemonic: You attempt to expel wind out of your mouth but lack the breath to blow out any. You’re using your mouth and trying to blow out some air, but you are failing to do so.
reading_mnemonic: You silly fool (ふ), the reason you couldn’t blow any air out of your mouth is because your hand was over it. You can’t blow air out that way. You silly fool, you.

meaning_mnemonic: The mole has a knife ready for your arrival. You get out of your airplane, you step on the ground and... ouch! You stepped right on the knife, and there's the mole, sticking it out of the ground. "I checked the schedule for your arrival!" it squeaks happily, and disappears.
reading_mnemonic: Your arrival to とうきょう is now ruined. And your next stop is now going to be an arrival at a とうきょう hospital to get this mole knife out.

meaning_mnemonic: Your long hair is your friend. It's your hair and you're so proud of it.
reading_mnemonic: Who gave you this hair? Probably the great 神 (かみ) of hair. You deserve this great hair.

meaning_mnemonic: I have sick in my skin. Just look at it, it doesn't look too good. Whenever I have sickness in my skin, I know that I'm probably tired.
reading_mnemonic: Why so tired? Your body is heated (ひ) up from exercising way too much. You should let that heat cool down so your skin starts looking better.

meaning_mnemonic: You have to stop keeping canines which are small once you reach a certain number of years old. You'll be hitting that age limit this year, which means your time with your small canine will end and you'll have to grow up and get a bigger one.
reading_mnemonic: Remember the vocab word 〜才 which also meant "years old"? Well, this has the same reading: さい.

meaning_mnemonic: The leader, Master Splinter (the rat from Ninja Turtles) isn't even supposed to exist. He exists because someone accidentally poured ooze on him.
reading_mnemonic: But really, if you do something accidentally, it's probably a good (ぐう) thing in a way. You learn a bit about how you can improve yourself so you don't do it again, or in Splinter's case, it's just a good mistake!

meaning_mnemonic: The leader of Korea is destined for greatness.
reading_mnemonic: The greatness radiates off of the leader of Korea, so much so that you can hardly look. Just when you're about to close your eyes to shield them from the greatness, a great eagle (い) soars over them, letting out a cry.

meaning_mnemonic: Take the street all the way to that geoduck, way up there. When you reach it, you will have made it to the summit. You humbly present the road to the geoduck and bow before it.
reading_mnemonic: You are at the top, the summit of everything! You humbly survey your surroundings from the top of the geoduck, only to see someone on the street, running toward you. It is Mrs. Chou (ちょう), and she looks angry.
